Job.34.32.bsb: Teach me what I cannot see; if I have done wrong, I will not do it again.’
Job.34.32.kjv: That which I see not teach thou me: if I have done iniquity, I will do no more.

Job.6.24.bsb: Teach me, and I will be silent. Help me understand how I have erred.
Job.6.24.kjv: Teach me, and I will hold my tongue: and cause me to understand wherein I have erred.

Job.10.2.bsb: I will say to God: Do not condemn me! Let me know why You prosecute me.
Job.10.2.kjv: I will say unto God, Do not condemn me; shew me wherefore thou contendest with me.

Job.13.23.bsb: How many are my iniquities and sins? Reveal to me my transgression and sin.
Job.13.23.kjv: How many are mine iniquities and sins? make me to know my transgression and my sin.

Job.13.24.bsb: Why do You hide Your face and consider me as Your enemy?
Job.13.24.kjv: Wherefore hidest thou thy face, and holdest me for thine enemy?

Job.38.7.bsb: while the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
Job.38.7.kjv: When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?

Job.25.3.bsb: Can His troops be numbered? On whom does His light not rise?
Job.25.3.kjv: Is there any number of his armies? and upon whom doth not his light arise?

Job.26.13.bsb: By His breath the skies were cleared; His hand pierced the fleeing serpent.
Job.26.13.kjv: By his spirit he hath garnished the heavens; his hand hath formed the crooked serpent.

Job.15.14.bsb: What is man, that he should be pure, or one born of woman, that he should be righteous?
Job.15.14.kjv: What is man, that he should be clean? and he which is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?

Job.25.4.bsb: How then can a man be just before God? How can one born of woman be pure?
Job.25.4.kjv: How then can man be justified with God? or how can he be clean that is born of a woman?

Job.11.12.bsb: But a witless man can no more become wise than the colt of a wild donkey can be born a man!
Job.11.12.kjv: For vain man would be wise, though man be born like a wild ass’s colt.

Job.15.16.bsb: how much less man, who is vile and corrupt, who drinks injustice like water?
Job.15.16.kjv: How much more abominable and filthy is man, which drinketh iniquity like water?

Job.5.6.bsb: For distress does not spring from the dust, and trouble does not sprout from the ground.
Job.5.6.kjv: Although affliction cometh not forth of the dust, neither doth trouble spring out of the ground;

Job.5.7.bsb: Yet man is born to trouble as surely as sparks fly upward.
Job.5.7.kjv: Yet man is born unto trouble, as the sparks fly upward.

Job.21.30.bsb: Indeed, the evil man is spared from the day of calamity, delivered from the day of wrath.
Job.21.30.kjv: That the wicked is reserved to the day of destruction? they shall be brought forth to the day of wrath.

Job.37.22.bsb: Out of the north He comes in golden splendor; awesome majesty surrounds Him.
Job.37.22.kjv: Fair weather cometh out of the north: with God is terrible majesty.

Job.12.12.bsb: Wisdom is found with the elderly, and understanding comes with long life.
Job.12.12.kjv: With the ancient is wisdom; and in length of days understanding.

Job.1.20.bsb: Then Job stood up, tore his robe, and shaved his head. He fell to the ground and worshiped,
Job.1.20.kjv: Then Job arose, and rent his mantle, and shaved his head, and fell down upon the ground, and worshipped,

Job.31.16.bsb: If I have denied the desires of the poor or allowed the widow’s eyes to fail,
Job.31.16.kjv: If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail;

Job.31.17.bsb: if I have eaten my morsel alone, not sharing it with the fatherless—
Job.31.17.kjv: Or have eaten my morsel myself alone, and the fatherless hath not eaten thereof;

Job.31.18.bsb: though from my youth I reared him as would a father, and from my mother’s womb I guided the widow—
Job.31.18.kjv: (For from my youth he was brought up with me, as with a father, and I have guided her from my mother’s womb;)

Job.31.19.bsb: if I have seen one perish for lack of clothing, or a needy man without a cloak,
Job.31.19.kjv: If I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or any poor without covering;

Job.31.20.bsb: if his heart has not blessed me for warming him with the fleece of my sheep,
Job.31.20.kjv: If his loins have not blessed me, and if he were not warmed with the fleece of my sheep;

Job.31.21.bsb: if I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless because I saw that I had support in the gate,
Job.31.21.kjv: If I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, when I saw my help in the gate:

Job.31.22.bsb: then may my arm fall from my shoulder and be torn from its socket.
Job.31.22.kjv: Then let mine arm fall from my shoulder blade, and mine arm be broken from the bone.

Job.22.2.bsb: “Can a man be of use to God? Can even a wise man benefit Him?
Job.22.2.kjv: Can a man be profitable unto God, as he that is wise may be profitable unto himself?

Job.7.17.bsb: What is man that You should exalt him, that You should set Your heart upon him,
Job.7.17.kjv: What is man, that thou shouldest magnify him? and that thou shouldest set thine heart upon him?

Job.33.4.bsb: The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
Job.33.4.kjv: The Spirit of God hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life.

Job.20.4.bsb: Do you not know that from antiquity, since man was placed on the earth,
Job.20.4.kjv: Knowest thou not this of old, since man was placed upon earth,

Job.33.6.bsb: I am just like you before God; I was also formed from clay.
Job.33.6.kjv: Behold, I am according to thy wish in God’s stead: I also am formed out of the clay.

Job.10.8.bsb: Your hands shaped me and altogether formed me. Would You now turn and destroy me?
Job.10.8.kjv: Thine hands have made me and fashioned me together round about; yet thou dost destroy me.

Job.10.9.bsb: Please remember that You molded me like clay. Would You now return me to dust?
Job.10.9.kjv: Remember, I beseech thee, that thou hast made me as the clay; and wilt thou bring me into dust again?

Job.10.10.bsb: Did You not pour me out like milk, and curdle me like cheese?
Job.10.10.kjv: Hast thou not poured me out as milk, and curdled me like cheese?

Job.10.11.bsb: You clothed me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews.
Job.10.11.kjv: Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh, and hast fenced me with bones and sinews.

Job.31.15.bsb: Did not He who made me in the womb also make them? Did not the same One form us in the womb?
Job.31.15.kjv: Did not he that made me in the womb make him? and did not one fashion us in the womb?

Job.32.8.bsb: But there is a spirit in a man, the breath of the Almighty, that gives him understanding.
Job.32.8.kjv: But there is a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding.

Job.32.9.bsb: It is not only the old who are wise, or the elderly who understand justice.
Job.32.9.kjv: Great men are not always wise: neither do the aged understand judgment.

Job.35.11.bsb: who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the air?’
Job.35.11.kjv: Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth, and maketh us wiser than the fowls of heaven?

Job.25.6.bsb: how much less man, who is but a maggot, and the son of man, who is but a worm!”
Job.25.6.kjv: How much less man, that is a worm? and the son of man, which is a worm?

Job.7.1.bsb: “Is not man consigned to labor on earth? Are not his days like those of a hired hand?
Job.7.1.kjv: Is there not an appointed time to man upon earth? are not his days also like the days of an hireling?

Job.14.1.bsb: “Man, who is born of woman, is short of days and full of trouble.
Job.14.1.kjv: Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble.

Job.7.20.bsb: If I have sinned, what have I done to You, O watcher of mankind? Why have You made me Your target, so that I am a burden to You?
Job.7.20.kjv: I have sinned; what shall I do unto thee, O thou preserver of men? why hast thou set me as a mark against thee, so that I am a burden to myself?

Job.14.19.bsb: as water wears away the stones and torrents wash away the soil, so You destroy a man’s hope.
Job.14.19.kjv: The waters wear the stones: thou washest away the things which grow out of the dust of the earth; and thou destroyest the hope of man.

Job.9.2.bsb: “Yes, I know that it is so, but how can a mortal be righteous before God?
Job.9.2.kjv: I know it is so of a truth: but how should man be just with God?

Job.2.4.bsb: “Skin for skin!” Satan replied. “A man will give up all he owns in exchange for his life.
Job.2.4.kjv: And Satan answered the Lord, and said, Skin for skin, yea, all that a man hath will he give for his life.

Job.8.5.bsb: But if you would earnestly seek God and ask the Almighty for mercy,
Job.8.5.kjv: If thou wouldest seek unto God betimes, and make thy supplication to the Almighty;

Job.11.13.bsb: As for you, if you direct your heart and lift up your hands to Him,
Job.11.13.kjv: If thou prepare thine heart, and stretch out thine hands toward him;

Job.22.23.bsb: If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored. If you remove injustice from your tents
Job.22.23.kjv: If thou return to the Almighty, thou shalt be built up, thou shalt put away iniquity far from thy tabernacles.

Job.22.27.bsb: You will pray to Him, and He will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows.
Job.22.27.kjv: Thou shalt make thy prayer unto him, and he shall hear thee, and thou shalt pay thy vows.

Job.27.8.bsb: For what is the hope of the godless when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?
Job.27.8.kjv: For what is the hope of the hypocrite, though he hath gained, when God taketh away his soul?

Job.27.9.bsb: Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him?
Job.27.9.kjv: Will God hear his cry when trouble cometh upon him?

Job.35.12.bsb: There they cry out, but He does not answer, because of the pride of evil men.
Job.35.12.kjv: There they cry, but none giveth answer, because of the pride of evil men.

Job.35.13.bsb: Surely God does not listen to empty pleas, and the Almighty does not take note of it.
Job.35.13.kjv: Surely God will not hear vanity, neither will the Almighty regard it.

Job.42.10.bsb: After Job had prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his prosperity and doubled his former possessions.
Job.42.10.kjv: And the Lord turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before.

Job.42.8.bsb: So now, take seven bulls and seven rams, go to My servant Job, and sacrifice a burnt offering for yourselves. Then My servant Job will pray for you, for I will accept his prayer and not deal with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken accurately about Me, as My servant Job has.”
Job.42.8.kjv: Therefore take unto you now seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you: for him will I accept: lest I deal with you after your folly, in that ye have not spoken of me the thing which is right, like my servant Job.

Job.1.5.bsb: And when the days of feasting were over, Job would send for his children to purify them, rising early in the morning to offer burnt offerings for all of them. For Job thought, “Perhaps my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts.” This was Job’s regular practice.
Job.1.5.kjv: And it was so, when the days of their feasting were gone about, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all: for Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.

Job.9.30.bsb: If I should wash myself with snow and cleanse my hands with lye,
Job.9.30.kjv: If I wash myself with snow water, and make my hands never so clean;

Job.9.31.bsb: then You would plunge me into the pit, and even my own clothes would despise me.
Job.9.31.kjv: Yet shalt thou plunge me in the ditch, and mine own clothes shall abhor me.

Job.4.15.bsb: Then a spirit glided past my face, and the hair on my body bristled.
Job.4.15.kjv: Then a spirit passed before my face; the hair of my flesh stood up:

Job.4.16.bsb: It stood still, but I could not discern its appearance; a form loomed before my eyes, and I heard a whispering voice:
Job.4.16.kjv: It stood still, but I could not discern the form thereof: an image was before mine eyes, there was silence, and I heard a voice, saying,

Job.4.17.bsb: ‘Can a mortal be more righteous than God, or a man more pure than his Maker?
Job.4.17.kjv: Shall mortal man be more just than God? shall a man be more pure than his maker?

Job.4.18.bsb: If God puts no trust in His servants, and He charges His angels with error,
Job.4.18.kjv: Behold, he put no trust in his servants; and his angels he charged with folly:

Job.4.19.bsb: how much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundations are in the dust, who can be crushed like a moth!
Job.4.19.kjv: How much less in them that dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, which are crushed before the moth?

Job.5.2.bsb: For resentment kills a fool, and envy slays the simple.
Job.5.2.kjv: For wrath killeth the foolish man, and envy slayeth the silly one.

Job.19.29.bsb: then you should fear the sword yourselves, because wrath brings punishment by the sword, so that you may know there is a judgment.”
Job.19.29.kjv: Be ye afraid of the sword: for wrath bringeth the punishments of the sword, that ye may know there is a judgment.

Job.32.3.bsb: and he burned with anger against Job’s three friends because they had failed to refute Job, and yet had condemned him.
Job.32.3.kjv: Also against his three friends was his wrath kindled, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.

Job.22.14.bsb: Thick clouds veil Him so He does not see us as He traverses the vault of heaven.’
Job.22.14.kjv: Thick clouds are a covering to him, that he seeth not; and he walketh in the circuit of heaven.

Job.34.26.bsb: He strikes them for their wickedness in full view,
Job.34.26.kjv: He striketh them as wicked men in the open sight of others;

Job.34.27.bsb: because they turned aside from Him and had no regard for any of His ways.
Job.34.27.kjv: Because they turned back from him, and would not consider any of his ways:

Job.22.24.bsb: and consign your gold to the dust and the gold of Ophir to the stones of the ravines,
Job.22.24.kjv: Then shalt thou lay up gold as dust, and the gold of Ophir as the stones of the brooks.

Job.22.25.bsb: then the Almighty will be your gold and the finest silver for you.
Job.22.25.kjv: Yea, the Almighty shall be thy defence, and thou shalt have plenty of silver.

Job.22.26.bsb: Surely then you will delight in the Almighty and lift up your face to God.
Job.22.26.kjv: For then shalt thou have thy delight in the Almighty, and shalt lift up thy face unto God.

Job.22.28.bsb: Your decisions will be carried out, and light will shine on your ways.
Job.22.28.kjv: Thou shalt also decree a thing, and it shall be established unto thee: and the light shall shine upon thy ways.

Job.22.29.bsb: When men are brought low and you say, ‘Lift them up!’ then He will save the lowly.
Job.22.29.kjv: When men are cast down, then thou shalt say, There is lifting up; and he shall save the humble person.

Job.22.30.bsb: He will deliver even one who is not innocent, rescuing him through the cleanness of your hands.”
Job.22.30.kjv: He shall deliver the island of the innocent: and it is delivered by the pureness of thine hands.

Job.29.11.bsb: For those who heard me called me blessed, and those who saw me commended me,
Job.29.11.kjv: When the ear heard me, then it blessed me; and when the eye saw me, it gave witness to me:

Job.29.12.bsb: because I rescued the poor who cried out and the fatherless who had no helper.
Job.29.12.kjv: Because I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and him that had none to help him.

Job.29.13.bsb: The dying man blessed me, and I made the widow’s heart sing for joy.
Job.29.13.kjv: The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me: and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.

Job.29.14.bsb: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; justice was my robe and my turban.
Job.29.14.kjv: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me: my judgment was as a robe and a diadem.

Job.29.15.bsb: I served as eyes to the blind and as feet to the lame.
Job.29.15.kjv: I was eyes to the blind, and feet was I to the lame.

Job.29.16.bsb: I was a father to the needy, and I took up the case of the stranger.
Job.29.16.kjv: I was a father to the poor: and the cause which I knew not I searched out.

Job.29.17.bsb: I shattered the fangs of the unjust and snatched the prey from his teeth.
Job.29.17.kjv: And I brake the jaws of the wicked, and plucked the spoil out of his teeth.

Job.31.23.bsb: For calamity from God terrifies me, and His splendor I cannot overpower.
Job.31.23.kjv: For destruction from God was a terror to me, and by reason of his highness I could not endure.

Job.9.16.bsb: If I summoned Him and He answered me, I do not believe He would listen to my voice.
Job.9.16.kjv: If I had called, and he had answered me; yet would I not believe that he had hearkened unto my voice.

Job.9.17.bsb: For He would crush me with a tempest and multiply my wounds without cause.
Job.9.17.kjv: For he breaketh me with a tempest, and multiplieth my wounds without cause.

Job.9.34.bsb: Let Him remove His rod from me, so that His terror will no longer frighten me.
Job.9.34.kjv: Let him take his rod away from me, and let not his fear terrify me:

Job.9.35.bsb: Then I would speak without fear of Him. But as it is, I am on my own.
Job.9.35.kjv: Then would I speak, and not fear him; but it is not so with me.

Job.10.3.bsb: Does it please You to oppress me, to reject the work of Your hands and favor the schemes of the wicked?
Job.10.3.kjv: Is it good unto thee that thou shouldest oppress, that thou shouldest despise the work of thine hands, and shine upon the counsel of the wicked?

Job.10.4.bsb: Do You have eyes of flesh? Do You see as man sees?
Job.10.4.kjv: Hast thou eyes of flesh? or seest thou as man seeth?

Job.10.5.bsb: Are Your days like those of a mortal, or Your years like those of a man,
Job.10.5.kjv: Are thy days as the days of man? are thy years as man’s days,

Job.10.6.bsb: that You should seek my iniquity and search out my sin—
Job.10.6.kjv: That thou enquirest after mine iniquity, and searchest after my sin?

Job.10.7.bsb: though You know that I am not guilty, and there is no deliverance from Your hand?
Job.10.7.kjv: Thou knowest that I am not wicked; and there is none that can deliver out of thine hand.

Job.13.7.bsb: Will you speak wickedly on God’s behalf or speak deceitfully for Him?
Job.13.7.kjv: Will ye speak wickedly for God? and talk deceitfully for him?

Job.13.8.bsb: Would you show Him partiality or argue in His defense?
Job.13.8.kjv: Will ye accept his person? will ye contend for God?

Job.13.9.bsb: Would it be well when He examined you? Could you deceive Him as you would deceive a man?
Job.13.9.kjv: Is it good that he should search you out? or as one man mocketh another, do ye so mock him?

Job.13.25.bsb: Would You frighten a windblown leaf? Would You chase after dry chaff?
Job.13.25.kjv: Wilt thou break a leaf driven to and fro? and wilt thou pursue the dry stubble?

Job.13.26.bsb: For You record bitter accusations against me and bequeath to me the iniquities of my youth.
Job.13.26.kjv: For thou writest bitter things against me, and makest me to possess the iniquities of my youth.

Job.13.27.bsb: You put my feet in the stocks and stand watch over all my paths; You set a limit for the soles of my feet.
Job.13.27.kjv: Thou puttest my feet also in the stocks, and lookest narrowly unto all my paths; thou settest a print upon the heels of my feet.

Job.15.13.bsb: so that you turn your spirit against God and pour such words from your mouth?
Job.15.13.kjv: That thou turnest thy spirit against God, and lettest such words go out of thy mouth?

Job.15.25.bsb: For he has stretched out his hand against God and has vaunted himself against the Almighty,
Job.15.25.kjv: For he stretcheth out his hand against God, and strengtheneth himself against the Almighty.

Job.15.26.bsb: rushing headlong at Him with a thick, studded shield.
Job.15.26.kjv: He runneth upon him, even on his neck, upon the thick bosses of his bucklers:

Job.16.9.bsb: His anger has torn me and opposed me; He gnashes His teeth at me. My adversary pierces me with His eyes.
Job.16.9.kjv: He teareth me in his wrath, who hateth me: he gnasheth upon me with his teeth; mine enemy sharpeneth his eyes upon me.

Job.16.11.bsb: God has delivered me to unjust men; He has thrown me to the clutches of the wicked.
Job.16.11.kjv: God hath delivered me to the ungodly, and turned me over into the hands of the wicked.

Job.16.14.bsb: He breaks me with wound upon wound; He rushes me like a mighty warrior.
Job.16.14.kjv: He breaketh me with breach upon breach, he runneth upon me like a giant.

Job.19.6.bsb: then understand that it is God who has wronged me and drawn His net around me.
Job.19.6.kjv: Know now that God hath overthrown me, and hath compassed me with his net.

Job.19.7.bsb: Though I cry out, ‘Violence!’ I get no response; though I call for help, there is no justice.
Job.19.7.kjv: Behold, I cry out of wrong, but I am not heard: I cry aloud, but there is no judgment.

Job.19.21.bsb: Have pity on me, my friends, have pity, for the hand of God has struck me.
Job.19.21.kjv: Have pity upon me, have pity upon me, O ye my friends; for the hand of God hath touched me.

Job.19.22.bsb: Why do you persecute me as God does? Will you never get enough of my flesh?
Job.19.22.kjv: Why do ye persecute me as God, and are not satisfied with my flesh?

Job.21.13.bsb: They spend their days in prosperity and go down to Sheol in peace.
Job.21.13.kjv: They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment go down to the grave.

Job.21.14.bsb: Yet they say to God: ‘Leave us alone! For we have no desire to know Your ways.
Job.21.14.kjv: Therefore they say unto God, Depart from us; for we desire not the knowledge of thy ways.

Job.22.12.bsb: Is not God as high as the heavens? Look at the highest stars, how lofty they are!
Job.22.12.kjv: Is not God in the height of heaven? and behold the height of the stars, how high they are!

Job.22.13.bsb: Yet you say: ‘What does God know? Does He judge through thick darkness?
Job.22.13.kjv: And thou sayest, How doth God know? can he judge through the dark cloud?

Job.22.17.bsb: They said to God, ‘Depart from us. What can the Almighty do to us?’
Job.22.17.kjv: Which said unto God, Depart from us: and what can the Almighty do for them?

Job.30.21.bsb: You have ruthlessly turned on me; You oppose me with Your strong hand.
Job.30.21.kjv: Thou art become cruel to me: with thy strong hand thou opposest thyself against me.

Job.33.10.bsb: Yet God finds occasions against me; He counts me as His enemy.
Job.33.10.kjv: Behold, he findeth occasions against me, he counteth me for his enemy,

Job.33.11.bsb: He puts my feet in the stocks; He watches over all my paths.’
Job.33.11.kjv: He putteth my feet in the stocks, he marketh all my paths.

Job.34.5.bsb: For Job has declared, ‘I am righteous, yet God has deprived me of justice.
Job.34.5.kjv: For Job hath said, I am righteous: and God hath taken away my judgment.

Job.34.6.bsb: Would I lie about my case? My wound is incurable, though I am without transgression.’
Job.34.6.kjv: Should I lie against my right? my wound is incurable without transgression.

Job.34.9.bsb: For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing that he should delight in God.’
Job.34.9.kjv: For he hath said, It profiteth a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.

Job.34.16.bsb: If you have understanding, hear this; listen to my words.
Job.34.16.kjv: If now thou hast understanding, hear this: hearken to the voice of my words.

Job.34.17.bsb: Could one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the just and mighty One,
Job.34.17.kjv: Shall even he that hateth right govern? and wilt thou condemn him that is most just?

Job.34.18.bsb: who says to kings, ‘You are worthless!’ and to nobles, ‘You are wicked,’
Job.34.18.kjv: Is it fit to say to a king, Thou art wicked? and to princes, Ye are ungodly?

Job.34.19.bsb: who is not partial to princes and does not favor rich over poor? For they are all the work of His hands.
Job.34.19.kjv: How much less to him that accepteth not the persons of princes, nor regardeth the rich more than the poor? for they all are the work of his hands.

Job.34.37.bsb: For he adds rebellion to his sin; he claps his hands among us and multiplies his words against God.”
Job.34.37.kjv: For he addeth rebellion unto his sin, he clappeth his hands among us, and multiplieth his words against God.

Job.37.20.bsb: Should He be told that I want to speak? Would a man ask to be swallowed up?
Job.37.20.kjv: Shall it be told him that I speak? if a man speak, surely he shall be swallowed up.

Job.40.2.bsb: “Will the faultfinder contend with the Almighty? Let him who argues with God give an answer.”
Job.40.2.kjv: Shall he that contendeth with the Almighty instruct him? he that reproveth God, let him answer it.

Job.2.9.bsb: Then Job’s wife said to him, “Do you still retain your integrity? Curse God and die!”
Job.2.9.kjv: Then said his wife unto him, Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die.

Job.5.25.bsb: You will know that your offspring will be many, your descendants like the grass of the earth.
Job.5.25.kjv: Thou shalt know also that thy seed shall be great, and thine offspring as the grass of the earth.

Job.24.9.bsb: The fatherless infant is snatched from the breast; the nursing child of the poor is seized for a debt.
Job.24.9.kjv: They pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor.

Job.21.19.bsb: It is said that God lays up one’s punishment for his children. Let God repay the man himself, so he will know it.
Job.21.19.kjv: God layeth up his iniquity for his children: he rewardeth him, and he shall know it.

Job.21.11.bsb: They send forth their little ones like a flock; their children skip about,
Job.21.11.kjv: They send forth their little ones like a flock, and their children dance.

Job.1.21.bsb: saying: “Naked I came from my mother’s womb, and naked I will return. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed be the name of the LORD.”
Job.1.21.kjv: And said, Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return thither: the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.

Job.32.6.bsb: So Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite declared: “I am young in years, while you are old; that is why I was timid and afraid to tell you what I know.
Job.32.6.kjv: And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, I am young, and ye are very old; wherefore I was afraid, and durst not shew you mine opinion.

Job.32.7.bsb: I thought that age should speak, and many years should teach wisdom.
Job.32.7.kjv: I said, Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom.

Job.29.4.bsb: when I was in my prime, when the friendship of God rested on my tent,
Job.29.4.kjv: As I was in the days of my youth, when the secret of God was upon my tabernacle;

Job.32.4.bsb: Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job because the others were older than he.
Job.32.4.kjv: Now Elihu had waited till Job had spoken, because they were elder than he.

Job.32.5.bsb: But when he saw that the three men had no further reply, his anger was kindled.
Job.32.5.kjv: When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, then his wrath was kindled.

Job.19.18.bsb: Even little boys scorn me; when I appear, they deride me.
Job.19.18.kjv: Yea, young children despised me; I arose, and they spake against me.

Job.20.11.bsb: The youthful vigor that fills his bones will lie down with him in the dust.
Job.20.11.kjv: His bones are full of the sin of his youth, which shall lie down with him in the dust.

Job.30.1.bsb: “But now they mock me, men younger than I am, whose fathers I would have refused to put with my sheep dogs.
Job.30.1.kjv: But now they that are younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I would have disdained to have set with the dogs of my flock.

Job.30.12.bsb: The rabble arises at my right; they lay snares for my feet and build siege ramps against me.
Job.30.12.kjv: Upon my right hand rise the youth; they push away my feet, and they raise up against me the ways of their destruction.

Job.18.14.bsb: He is torn from the shelter of his tent and is marched off to the king of terrors.
Job.18.14.kjv: His confidence shall be rooted out of his tabernacle, and it shall bring him to the king of terrors.

Job.14.14.bsb: When a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard service I will wait, until my renewal comes.
Job.14.14.kjv: If a man die, shall he live again? all the days of my appointed time will I wait, till my change come.

Job.16.22.bsb: For when only a few years are past I will go the way of no return.
Job.16.22.kjv: When a few years are come, then I shall go the way whence I shall not return.

Job.14.2.bsb: Like a flower, he comes forth, then withers away; like a fleeting shadow, he does not endure.
Job.14.2.kjv: He cometh forth like a flower, and is cut down: he fleeth also as a shadow, and continueth not.

Job.7.21.bsb: Why do You not pardon my transgression and take away my iniquity? For soon I will lie down in the dust; You will seek me, but I will be no more.”
Job.7.21.kjv: And why dost thou not pardon my transgression, and take away mine iniquity? for now shall I sleep in the dust; and thou shalt seek me in the morning, but I shall not be.

Job.14.12.bsb: so a man lies down and does not rise. Until the heavens are no more, he will not be awakened or roused from sleep.
Job.14.12.kjv: So man lieth down, and riseth not: till the heavens be no more, they shall not awake, nor be raised out of their sleep.

Job.6.8.bsb: If only my request were granted and God would fulfill my hope:
Job.6.8.kjv: Oh that I might have my request; and that God would grant me the thing that I long for!

Job.6.9.bsb: that God would be willing to crush me, to unleash His hand and cut me off!
Job.6.9.kjv: Even that it would please God to destroy me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!

Job.6.10.bsb: It still brings me comfort, and joy through unrelenting pain, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
Job.6.10.kjv: Then should I yet have comfort; yea, I would harden myself in sorrow: let him not spare; for I have not concealed the words of the Holy One.

Job.6.11.bsb: What strength do I have, that I should still hope? What is my future, that I should be patient?
Job.6.11.kjv: What is my strength, that I should hope? and what is mine end, that I should prolong my life?

Job.7.2.bsb: Like a slave he longs for shade; like a hireling he waits for his wages.
Job.7.2.kjv: As a servant earnestly desireth the shadow, and as an hireling looketh for the reward of his work:

Job.7.3.bsb: So I am allotted months of futility, and nights of misery are appointed to me.
Job.7.3.kjv: So am I made to possess months of vanity, and wearisome nights are appointed to me.

Job.7.15.bsb: so that I would prefer strangling and death over my life in this body.
Job.7.15.kjv: So that my soul chooseth strangling, and death rather than my life.

Job.7.16.bsb: I loathe my life! I would not live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.
Job.7.16.kjv: I loathe it; I would not live alway: let me alone; for my days are vanity.

Job.10.1.bsb: “I loathe my own life; I will express my complaint and speak in the bitterness of my soul.
Job.10.1.kjv: My soul is weary of my life; I will leave my complaint upon myself; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.

Job.14.13.bsb: If only You would hide me in Sheol and conceal me until Your anger has passed! If only You would appoint a time for me and then remember me!
Job.14.13.kjv: O that thou wouldest hide me in the grave, that thou wouldest keep me secret, until thy wrath be past, that thou wouldest appoint me a set time, and remember me!

Job.3.13.bsb: For now I would be lying down in peace; I would be asleep and at rest
Job.3.13.kjv: For now should I have lain still and been quiet, I should have slept: then had I been at rest,

Job.3.17.bsb: There the wicked cease from raging, and there the weary find rest.
Job.3.17.kjv: There the wicked cease from troubling; and there the weary be at rest.

Job.3.18.bsb: The captives enjoy their ease; they do not hear the voice of the oppressor.
Job.3.18.kjv: There the prisoners rest together; they hear not the voice of the oppressor.

Job.3.19.bsb: Both small and great are there, and the slave is freed from his master.
Job.3.19.kjv: The small and great are there; and the servant is free from his master.

Job.7.8.bsb: The eye that beholds me will no longer see me. You will look for me, but I will be no more.
Job.7.8.kjv: The eye of him that hath seen me shall see me no more: thine eyes are upon me, and I am not.

Job.7.9.bsb: As a cloud vanishes and is gone, so he who goes down to Sheol does not come back up.
Job.7.9.kjv: As the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away: so he that goeth down to the grave shall come up no more.

Job.7.10.bsb: He never returns to his house; his place remembers him no more.
Job.7.10.kjv: He shall return no more to his house, neither shall his place know him any more.

Job.10.21.bsb: before I go—never to return—to a land of darkness and gloom,
Job.10.21.kjv: Before I go whence I shall not return, even to the land of darkness and the shadow of death;

Job.10.22.bsb: to a land of utter darkness, of deep shadow and disorder, where even the light is like darkness.”
Job.10.22.kjv: A land of darkness, as darkness itself; and of the shadow of death, without any order, and where the light is as darkness.

Job.14.5.bsb: Since his days are determined and the number of his months is with You, and since You have set limits that he cannot exceed,
Job.14.5.kjv: Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months are with thee, thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass;

Job.14.6.bsb: look away from him and let him rest, so he can enjoy his day as a hired hand.
Job.14.6.kjv: Turn from him, that he may rest, till he shall accomplish, as an hireling, his day.

Job.14.7.bsb: For there is hope for a tree: If it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its tender shoots will not fail.
Job.14.7.kjv: For there is hope of a tree, if it be cut down, that it will sprout again, and that the tender branch thereof will not cease.

Job.14.8.bsb: If its roots grow old in the ground and its stump dies in the soil,
Job.14.8.kjv: Though the root thereof wax old in the earth, and the stock thereof die in the ground;

Job.14.9.bsb: at the scent of water it will bud and put forth twigs like a sapling.
Job.14.9.kjv: Yet through the scent of water it will bud, and bring forth boughs like a plant.

Job.14.10.bsb: But a man dies and is laid low; he breathes his last, and where is he?
Job.14.10.kjv: But man dieth, and wasteth away: yea, man giveth up the ghost, and where is he?

Job.14.11.bsb: As water disappears from the sea and a river becomes parched and dry,
Job.14.11.kjv: As the waters fail from the sea, and the flood decayeth and drieth up:

Job.14.20.bsb: You forever overpower him, and he passes on; You change his countenance and send him away.
Job.14.20.kjv: Thou prevailest for ever against him, and he passeth: thou changest his countenance, and sendest him away.

Job.14.21.bsb: If his sons receive honor, he does not know it; if they are brought low, he is unaware.
Job.14.21.kjv: His sons come to honour, and he knoweth it not; and they are brought low, but he perceiveth it not of them.

Job.17.13.bsb: If I look for Sheol as my home, if I spread out my bed in darkness,
Job.17.13.kjv: If I wait, the grave is mine house: I have made my bed in the darkness.

Job.17.14.bsb: and say to corruption, ‘You are my father,’ and to the worm, ‘My mother,’ or ‘My sister,’
Job.17.14.kjv: I have said to corruption, Thou art my father: to the worm, Thou art my mother, and my sister.

Job.17.16.bsb: Will it go down to the gates of Sheol? Will we go down together into the dust?”
Job.17.16.kjv: They shall go down to the bars of the pit, when our rest together is in the dust.

Job.21.23.bsb: One man dies full of vigor, completely secure and at ease.
Job.21.23.kjv: One dieth in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet.

Job.21.25.bsb: Yet another man dies in the bitterness of his soul, having never tasted prosperity.
Job.21.25.kjv: And another dieth in the bitterness of his soul, and never eateth with pleasure.

Job.21.26.bsb: But together they lie down in the dust, and worms cover them both.
Job.21.26.kjv: They shall lie down alike in the dust, and the worms shall cover them.

Job.21.32.bsb: He is carried to the grave, and watch is kept over his tomb.
Job.21.32.kjv: Yet shall he be brought to the grave, and shall remain in the tomb.

Job.21.33.bsb: The clods of the valley are sweet to him; everyone follows behind him, and those before him are without number.
Job.21.33.kjv: The clods of the valley shall be sweet unto him, and every man shall draw after him, as there are innumerable before him.

Job.30.23.bsb: Yes, I know that You will bring me down to death, to the place appointed for all the living.
Job.30.23.kjv: For I know that thou wilt bring me to death, and to the house appointed for all living.

Job.34.14.bsb: If He were to set His heart to it and withdraw His Spirit and breath,
Job.34.14.kjv: If he set his heart upon man, if he gather unto himself his spirit and his breath;

Job.34.15.bsb: all flesh would perish together and mankind would return to the dust.
Job.34.15.kjv: All flesh shall perish together, and man shall turn again unto dust.

Job.36.18.bsb: Be careful that no one lures you with riches; do not let a large bribe lead you astray.
Job.36.18.kjv: Because there is wrath, beware lest he take thee away with his stroke: then a great ransom cannot deliver thee.

Job.36.19.bsb: Can your wealth or all your mighty effort keep you from distress?
Job.36.19.kjv: Will he esteem thy riches? no, not gold, nor all the forces of strength.

Job.38.17.bsb: Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?
Job.38.17.kjv: Have the gates of death been opened unto thee? or hast thou seen the doors of the shadow of death?

Job.4.21.bsb: Are not their tent cords pulled up, so that they die without wisdom?’
Job.4.21.kjv: Doth not their excellency which is in them go away? they die, even without wisdom.

Job.18.18.bsb: He is driven from light into darkness and is chased from the inhabited world.
Job.18.18.kjv: He shall be driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the world.

Job.20.5.bsb: the triumph of the wicked has been brief and the joy of the godless momentary?
Job.20.5.kjv: That the triumphing of the wicked is short, and the joy of the hypocrite but for a moment?

Job.20.8.bsb: He will fly away like a dream, never to be found; he will be chased away like a vision in the night.
Job.20.8.kjv: He shall fly away as a dream, and shall not be found: yea, he shall be chased away as a vision of the night.

Job.21.17.bsb: How often is the lamp of the wicked put out? Does disaster come upon them? Does God, in His anger, apportion destruction?
Job.21.17.kjv: How oft is the candle of the wicked put out! and how oft cometh their destruction upon them! God distributeth sorrows in his anger.

Job.21.18.bsb: Are they like straw before the wind, like chaff swept away by a storm?
Job.21.18.kjv: They are as stubble before the wind, and as chaff that the storm carrieth away.

Job.21.24.bsb: His body is well nourished, and his bones are rich with marrow.
Job.21.24.kjv: His breasts are full of milk, and his bones are moistened with marrow.

Job.24.20.bsb: The womb forgets them; the worm feeds on them; they are remembered no more. So injustice is broken like a tree.
Job.24.20.kjv: The womb shall forget him; the worm shall feed sweetly on him; he shall be no more remembered; and wickedness shall be broken as a tree.

Job.24.24.bsb: They are exalted for a moment, then they are gone; they are brought low and gathered up like all others; they are cut off like heads of grain.
Job.24.24.kjv: They are exalted for a little while, but are gone and brought low; they are taken out of the way as all other, and cut off as the tops of the ears of corn.

Job.27.19.bsb: He lies down wealthy, but will do so no more; when he opens his eyes, all is gone.
Job.27.19.kjv: The rich man shall lie down, but he shall not be gathered: he openeth his eyes, and he is not.

Job.27.20.bsb: Terrors overtake him like a flood; a tempest sweeps him away in the night.
Job.27.20.kjv: Terrors take hold on him as waters, a tempest stealeth him away in the night.

Job.27.21.bsb: The east wind carries him away, and he is gone; it sweeps him out of his place.
Job.27.21.kjv: The east wind carrieth him away, and he departeth: and as a storm hurleth him out of his place.

Job.27.22.bsb: It hurls itself against him without mercy as he flees headlong from its power.
Job.27.22.kjv: For God shall cast upon him, and not spare: he would fain flee out of his hand.

Job.27.23.bsb: It claps its hands at him and hisses him out of his place.
Job.27.23.kjv: Men shall clap their hands at him, and shall hiss him out of his place.

Job.34.20.bsb: They die in an instant, in the middle of the night. The people convulse and pass away; the mighty are removed without human hand.
Job.34.20.kjv: In a moment shall they die, and the people shall be troubled at midnight, and pass away: and the mighty shall be taken away without hand.

Job.36.12.bsb: But if they do not obey, then they perish by the sword and die without knowledge.
Job.36.12.kjv: But if they obey not, they shall perish by the sword, and they shall die without knowledge.

Job.36.14.bsb: They die in their youth, among the male shrine prostitutes.
Job.36.14.kjv: They die in youth, and their life is among the unclean.

Job.36.20.bsb: Do not long for the night, when people vanish from their homes.
Job.36.20.kjv: Desire not the night, when people are cut off in their place.

Job.9.3.bsb: If one wished to contend with God, he could not answer Him one time out of a thousand.
Job.9.3.kjv: If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one of a thousand.

Job.9.20.bsb: Even if I were righteous, my mouth would condemn me; if I were blameless, it would declare me guilty.
Job.9.20.kjv: If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me: if I say, I am perfect, it shall also prove me perverse.

Job.9.29.bsb: Since I am already found guilty, why should I labor in vain?
Job.9.29.kjv: If I be wicked, why then labour I in vain?

Job.14.4.bsb: Who can bring out clean from unclean? No one!
Job.14.4.kjv: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? not one.

Job.15.15.bsb: If God puts no trust in His holy ones, if even the heavens are not pure in His eyes,
Job.15.15.kjv: Behold, he putteth no trust in his saints; yea, the heavens are not clean in his sight.

Job.25.5.bsb: If even the moon does not shine, and the stars are not pure in His sight,
Job.25.5.kjv: Behold even to the moon, and it shineth not; yea, the stars are not pure in his sight.

Job.5.3.bsb: I have seen a fool taking root, but suddenly his house was cursed.
Job.5.3.kjv: I have seen the foolish taking root: but suddenly I cursed his habitation.

Job.35.14.bsb: How much less, then, when you say that you do not see Him, that your case is before Him and you must wait for Him,
Job.35.14.kjv: Although thou sayest thou shalt not see him, yet judgment is before him; therefore trust thou in him.

Job.4.7.bsb: Consider now, I plead: Who, being innocent, has ever perished? Or where have the upright been destroyed?
Job.4.7.kjv: Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished, being innocent? or where were the righteous cut off?

Job.4.8.bsb: As I have observed, those who plow iniquity and those who sow trouble reap the same.
Job.4.8.kjv: Even as I have seen, they that plow iniquity, and sow wickedness, reap the same.

Job.4.9.bsb: By the breath of God they perish, and by the blast of His anger they are consumed.
Job.4.9.kjv: By the blast of God they perish, and by the breath of his nostrils are they consumed.

Job.4.10.bsb: The lion may roar, and the fierce lion may growl, yet the teeth of the young lions are broken.
Job.4.10.kjv: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, and the teeth of the young lions, are broken.

Job.4.11.bsb: The old lion perishes for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness are scattered.
Job.4.11.kjv: The old lion perisheth for lack of prey, and the stout lion’s whelps are scattered abroad.

Job.4.12.bsb: Now a word came to me secretly; my ears caught a whisper of it.
Job.4.12.kjv: Now a thing was secretly brought to me, and mine ear received a little thereof.

Job.4.13.bsb: In disquieting visions in the night, when deep sleep falls on men,
Job.4.13.kjv: In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falleth on men,

Job.4.14.bsb: fear and trembling came over me and made all my bones shudder.
Job.4.14.kjv: Fear came upon me, and trembling, which made all my bones to shake.

Job.4.20.bsb: They are smashed to pieces from dawn to dusk; unnoticed, they perish forever.
Job.4.20.kjv: They are destroyed from morning to evening: they perish for ever without any regarding it.

Job.5.8.bsb: However, if I were you, I would appeal to God and lay my cause before Him—
Job.5.8.kjv: I would seek unto God, and unto God would I commit my cause:

Job.5.9.bsb: the One who does great and unsearchable things, wonders without number.
Job.5.9.kjv: Which doeth great things and unsearchable; marvellous things without number:

Job.10.12.bsb: You have granted me life and loving devotion, and Your care has preserved my spirit.
Job.10.12.kjv: Thou hast granted me life and favour, and thy visitation hath preserved my spirit.

Job.13.15.bsb: Though He slay me, I will hope in Him. I will still defend my ways to His face.
Job.13.15.kjv: Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him: but I will maintain mine own ways before him.

Job.14.15.bsb: You will call, and I will answer; You will desire the work of Your hands.
Job.14.15.kjv: Thou shalt call, and I will answer thee: thou wilt have a desire to the work of thine hands.

Job.16.19.bsb: Even now my witness is in heaven, and my advocate is on high.
Job.16.19.kjv: Also now, behold, my witness is in heaven, and my record is on high.

Job.19.25.bsb: But I know that my Redeemer lives, and in the end He will stand upon the earth.
Job.19.25.kjv: For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth:

Job.19.26.bsb: Even after my skin has been destroyed, yet in my flesh I will see God.
Job.19.26.kjv: And though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God:

Job.19.27.bsb: I will see Him for myself; my eyes will behold Him, and not as a stranger. How my heart yearns within me!
Job.19.27.kjv: Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another; though my reins be consumed within me.

Job.23.6.bsb: Would He contend with me in His great power? No, He would certainly take note of me.
Job.23.6.kjv: Will he plead against me with his great power? No; but he would put strength in me.

Job.42.2.bsb: “I know that You can do all things and that no plan of Yours can be thwarted.
Job.42.2.kjv: I know that thou canst do every thing, and that no thought can be withholden from thee.

Job.5.10.bsb: He gives rain to the earth and sends water upon the fields.
Job.5.10.kjv: Who giveth rain upon the earth, and sendeth waters upon the fields:

Job.5.11.bsb: He sets the lowly on high, so that mourners are lifted to safety.
Job.5.11.kjv: To set up on high those that be low; that those which mourn may be exalted to safety.

Job.5.12.bsb: He thwarts the schemes of the crafty, so that their hands find no success.
Job.5.12.kjv: He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform their enterprise.

Job.5.13.bsb: He catches the wise in their craftiness, and sweeps away the plans of the cunning.
Job.5.13.kjv: He taketh the wise in their own craftiness: and the counsel of the froward is carried headlong.

Job.5.14.bsb: They encounter darkness by day and grope at noon as in the night.
Job.5.14.kjv: They meet with darkness in the daytime, and grope in the noonday as in the night.

Job.5.15.bsb: He saves the needy from the sword in their mouth and from the clutches of the powerful.
Job.5.15.kjv: But he saveth the poor from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty.

Job.5.16.bsb: So the poor have hope, and injustice shuts its mouth.
Job.5.16.kjv: So the poor hath hope, and iniquity stoppeth her mouth.

Job.5.17.bsb: Blessed indeed is the man whom God corrects; so do not despise the discipline of the Almighty.
Job.5.17.kjv: Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth: therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty:

Job.5.18.bsb: For He wounds, but He also binds; He strikes, but His hands also heal.
Job.5.18.kjv: For he maketh sore, and bindeth up: he woundeth, and his hands make whole.

Job.5.19.bsb: He will rescue you from six calamities; no harm will touch you in seven.
Job.5.19.kjv: He shall deliver thee in six troubles: yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee.

Job.5.20.bsb: In famine He will redeem you from death, and in battle from the stroke of the sword.
Job.5.20.kjv: In famine he shall redeem thee from death: and in war from the power of the sword.

Job.5.21.bsb: You will be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, and will not fear havoc when it comes.
Job.5.21.kjv: Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue: neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh.

Job.5.22.bsb: You will laugh at destruction and famine, and need not fear the beasts of the earth.
Job.5.22.kjv: At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh: neither shalt thou be afraid of the beasts of the earth.

Job.5.23.bsb: For you will have a covenant with the stones of the field, and the wild animals will be at peace with you.
Job.5.23.kjv: For thou shalt be in league with the stones of the field: and the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee.

Job.5.24.bsb: You will know that your tent is secure, and find nothing amiss when inspecting your home.
Job.5.24.kjv: And thou shalt know that thy tabernacle shall be in peace; and thou shalt visit thy habitation, and shalt not sin.

Job.5.26.bsb: You will come to the grave in full vigor, like a sheaf of grain gathered in season.
Job.5.26.kjv: Thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age, like as a shock of corn cometh in in his season.

Job.5.27.bsb: Indeed, we have investigated, and it is true! So hear it and know for yourself.”
Job.5.27.kjv: Lo this, we have searched it, so it is; hear it, and know thou it for thy good.

Job.31.33.bsb: if I have covered my transgressions like Adam by hiding my guilt in my heart,
Job.31.33.kjv: If I covered my transgressions as Adam, by hiding mine iniquity in my bosom:

Job.35.10.bsb: But no one asks, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives us songs in the night,
Job.35.10.kjv: But none saith, Where is God my maker, who giveth songs in the night;

Job.9.4.bsb: God is wise in heart and mighty in strength. Who has resisted Him and prospered?
Job.9.4.kjv: He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who hath hardened himself against him, and hath prospered?

Job.9.5.bsb: He moves mountains without their knowledge and overturns them in His anger.
Job.9.5.kjv: Which removeth the mountains, and they know not: which overturneth them in his anger.

Job.9.6.bsb: He shakes the earth from its place, so that its foundations tremble.
Job.9.6.kjv: Which shaketh the earth out of her place, and the pillars thereof tremble.

Job.9.7.bsb: He commands the sun not to shine; He seals off the stars.
Job.9.7.kjv: Which commandeth the sun, and it riseth not; and sealeth up the stars.

Job.9.8.bsb: He alone stretches out the heavens and treads on the waves of the sea.
Job.9.8.kjv: Which alone spreadeth out the heavens, and treadeth upon the waves of the sea.

Job.9.9.bsb: He is the Maker of the Bear and Orion, of the Pleiades and the constellations of the south.
Job.9.9.kjv: Which maketh Arcturus, Orion, and Pleiades, and the chambers of the south.

Job.9.10.bsb: He does great things beyond searching out, and wonders without number.
Job.9.10.kjv: Which doeth great things past finding out; yea, and wonders without number.

Job.9.11.bsb: Were He to pass by me, I would not see Him; were He to move, I would not recognize Him.
Job.9.11.kjv: Lo, he goeth by me, and I see him not: he passeth on also, but I perceive him not.

Job.9.12.bsb: If He takes away, who can stop Him? Who dares to ask Him, ‘What are You doing?’
Job.9.12.kjv: Behold, he taketh away, who can hinder him? who will say unto him, What doest thou?

Job.9.13.bsb: God does not restrain His anger; the helpers of Rahab cower beneath Him.
Job.9.13.kjv: If God will not withdraw his anger, the proud helpers do stoop under him.

Job.9.14.bsb: How then can I answer Him or choose my arguments against Him?
Job.9.14.kjv: How much less shall I answer him, and choose out my words to reason with him?

Job.9.15.bsb: For even if I were right, I could not answer. I could only beg my Judge for mercy.
Job.9.15.kjv: Whom, though I were righteous, yet would I not answer, but I would make supplication to my judge.

Job.9.18.bsb: He does not let me catch my breath, but overwhelms me with bitterness.
Job.9.18.kjv: He will not suffer me to take my breath, but filleth me with bitterness.

Job.9.19.bsb: If it is a matter of strength, He is indeed mighty! If it is a matter of justice, who can summon Him?
Job.9.19.kjv: If I speak of strength, lo, he is strong: and if of judgment, who shall set me a time to plead?

Job.9.21.bsb: Though I am blameless, I have no concern for myself; I despise my own life.
Job.9.21.kjv: Though I were perfect, yet would I not know my soul: I would despise my life.

Job.9.22.bsb: It is all the same, and so I say, ‘He destroys both the blameless and the wicked.’
Job.9.22.kjv: This is one thing, therefore I said it, He destroyeth the perfect and the wicked.

Job.9.23.bsb: When the scourge brings sudden death, He mocks the despair of the innocent.
Job.9.23.kjv: If the scourge slay suddenly, he will laugh at the trial of the innocent.

Job.9.24.bsb: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; He blindfolds its judges. If it is not He, then who is it?
Job.9.24.kjv: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof; if not, where, and who is he?

Job.9.25.bsb: My days are swifter than a runner; they flee without seeing good.
Job.9.25.kjv: Now my days are swifter than a post: they flee away, they see no good.

Job.9.26.bsb: They sweep by like boats of papyrus, like an eagle swooping down on its prey.
Job.9.26.kjv: They are passed away as the swift ships: as the eagle that hasteth to the prey.

Job.9.27.bsb: If I were to say, ‘I will forget my complaint and change my expression and smile,’
Job.9.27.kjv: If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will leave off my heaviness, and comfort myself:

Job.9.28.bsb: I would still dread all my sufferings; I know that You will not acquit me.
Job.9.28.kjv: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that thou wilt not hold me innocent.

Job.9.32.bsb: For He is not a man like me, that I can answer Him, that we can take each other to court.
Job.9.32.kjv: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, and we should come together in judgment.

Job.9.33.bsb: Nor is there a mediator between us, to lay his hand upon us both.
Job.9.33.kjv: Neither is there any daysman betwixt us, that might lay his hand upon us both.

Job.10.13.bsb: Yet You concealed these things in Your heart, and I know that this was in Your mind:
Job.10.13.kjv: And these things hast thou hid in thine heart: I know that this is with thee.

Job.10.14.bsb: If I sinned, You would take note, and would not acquit me of my iniquity.
Job.10.14.kjv: If I sin, then thou markest me, and thou wilt not acquit me from mine iniquity.

Job.10.15.bsb: If I am guilty, woe to me! And even if I am righteous, I cannot lift my head. I am full of shame and aware of my affliction.
Job.10.15.kjv: If I be wicked, woe unto me; and if I be righteous, yet will I not lift up my head. I am full of confusion; therefore see thou mine affliction;

Job.10.16.bsb: Should I hold my head high, You would hunt me like a lion, and again display Your power against me.
Job.10.16.kjv: For it increaseth. Thou huntest me as a fierce lion: and again thou shewest thyself marvellous upon me.

Job.10.17.bsb: You produce new witnesses against me and multiply Your anger toward me. Hardships assault me in wave after wave.
Job.10.17.kjv: Thou renewest thy witnesses against me, and increasest thine indignation upon me; changes and war are against me.

Job.10.18.bsb: Why then did You bring me from the womb? Oh, that I had died, and no eye had seen me!
Job.10.18.kjv: Wherefore then hast thou brought me forth out of the womb? Oh that I had given up the ghost, and no eye had seen me!

Job.12.7.bsb: But ask the animals, and they will instruct you; ask the birds of the air, and they will tell you.
Job.12.7.kjv: But ask now the beasts, and they shall teach thee; and the fowls of the air, and they shall tell thee:

Job.12.8.bsb: Or speak to the earth, and it will teach you; let the fish of the sea inform you.
Job.12.8.kjv: Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach thee: and the fishes of the sea shall declare unto thee.

Job.12.9.bsb: Which of all these does not know that the hand of the LORD has done this?
Job.12.9.kjv: Who knoweth not in all these that the hand of the Lord hath wrought this?

Job.12.10.bsb: The life of every living thing is in His hand, as well as the breath of all mankind.
Job.12.10.kjv: In whose hand is the soul of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind.

Job.12.11.bsb: Does not the ear test words as the tongue tastes its food?
Job.12.11.kjv: Doth not the ear try words? and the mouth taste his meat?

Job.12.13.bsb: Wisdom and strength belong to God; counsel and understanding are His.
Job.12.13.kjv: With him is wisdom and strength, he hath counsel and understanding.

Job.12.14.bsb: What He tears down cannot be rebuilt; the man He imprisons cannot be released.
Job.12.14.kjv: Behold, he breaketh down, and it cannot be built again: he shutteth up a man, and there can be no opening.

Job.12.15.bsb: If He holds back the waters, they dry up, and if He releases them, they overwhelm the land.
Job.12.15.kjv: Behold, he withholdeth the waters, and they dry up: also he sendeth them out, and they overturn the earth.

Job.12.16.bsb: True wisdom and power belong to Him. The deceived and the deceiver are His.
Job.12.16.kjv: With him is strength and wisdom: the deceived and the deceiver are his.

Job.12.17.bsb: He leads counselors away barefoot and makes fools of judges.
Job.12.17.kjv: He leadeth counsellors away spoiled, and maketh the judges fools.

Job.12.18.bsb: He loosens the bonds placed by kings and fastens a belt around their waists.
Job.12.18.kjv: He looseth the bond of kings, and girdeth their loins with a girdle.

Job.12.19.bsb: He leads priests away barefoot and overthrows the established.
Job.12.19.kjv: He leadeth princes away spoiled, and overthroweth the mighty.

Job.12.20.bsb: He deprives the trusted of speech and takes away the discernment of elders.
Job.12.20.kjv: He removeth away the speech of the trusty, and taketh away the understanding of the aged.

Job.26.7.bsb: He stretches out the north over empty space; He hangs the earth upon nothing.
Job.26.7.kjv: He stretcheth out the north over the empty place, and hangeth the earth upon nothing.

Job.26.8.bsb: He wraps up the waters in His clouds, yet the clouds do not burst under their own weight.
Job.26.8.kjv: He bindeth up the waters in his thick clouds; and the cloud is not rent under them.

Job.26.9.bsb: He covers the face of the full moon, spreading over it His cloud.
Job.26.9.kjv: He holdeth back the face of his throne, and spreadeth his cloud upon it.

Job.26.10.bsb: He has inscribed a horizon on the face of the waters at the boundary between light and darkness.
Job.26.10.kjv: He hath compassed the waters with bounds, until the day and night come to an end.

Job.26.11.bsb: The foundations of heaven quake, astounded at His rebuke.
Job.26.11.kjv: The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his reproof.

Job.26.12.bsb: By His power He stirred the sea; by His understanding He shattered Rahab.
Job.26.12.kjv: He divideth the sea with his power, and by his understanding he smiteth through the proud.

Job.26.14.bsb: Indeed, these are but the fringes of His ways; how faint is the whisper we hear of Him! Who then can understand the thunder of His power?”
Job.26.14.kjv: Lo, these are parts of his ways: but how little a portion is heard of him? but the thunder of his power who can understand?

Job.33.12.bsb: Behold, you are not right in this matter. I will answer you, for God is greater than man.
Job.33.12.kjv: Behold, in this thou art not just: I will answer thee, that God is greater than man.

Job.33.13.bsb: Why do you complain to Him that He answers nothing a man asks?
Job.33.13.kjv: Why dost thou strive against him? for he giveth not account of any of his matters.

Job.33.14.bsb: For God speaks in one way and in another, yet no one notices.
Job.33.14.kjv: For God speaketh once, yea twice, yet man perceiveth it not.

Job.33.15.bsb: In a dream, in a vision in the night, when deep sleep falls upon men as they slumber on their beds,
Job.33.15.kjv: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falleth upon men, in slumberings upon the bed;

Job.33.16.bsb: He opens their ears and terrifies them with warnings
Job.33.16.kjv: Then he openeth the ears of men, and sealeth their instruction,

Job.33.17.bsb: to turn a man from wrongdoing and keep him from pride,
Job.33.17.kjv: That he may withdraw man from his purpose, and hide pride from man.

Job.33.18.bsb: to preserve his soul from the Pit and his life from perishing by the sword.
Job.33.18.kjv: He keepeth back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.

Job.33.19.bsb: A man is also chastened on his bed with pain and constant distress in his bones,
Job.33.19.kjv: He is chastened also with pain upon his bed, and the multitude of his bones with strong pain:

Job.33.20.bsb: so that he detests his bread, and his soul loathes his favorite food.
Job.33.20.kjv: So that his life abhorreth bread, and his soul dainty meat.

Job.33.21.bsb: His flesh wastes away from sight, and his hidden bones protrude.
Job.33.21.kjv: His flesh is consumed away, that it cannot be seen; and his bones that were not seen stick out.

Job.33.22.bsb: He draws near to the Pit, and his life to the messengers of death.
Job.33.22.kjv: Yea, his soul draweth near unto the grave, and his life to the destroyers.

Job.33.23.bsb: Yet if there is a messenger on his side, one mediator in a thousand, to tell a man what is right for him,
Job.33.23.kjv: If there be a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to shew unto man his uprightness:

Job.33.24.bsb: to be gracious to him and say, ‘Spare him from going down to the Pit; I have found his ransom,’
Job.33.24.kjv: Then he is gracious unto him, and saith, Deliver him from going down to the pit: I have found a ransom.

Job.33.25.bsb: then his flesh is refreshed like a child’s; he returns to the days of his youth.
Job.33.25.kjv: His flesh shall be fresher than a child’s: he shall return to the days of his youth:

Job.33.26.bsb: He prays to God and finds favor; he sees God’s face and shouts for joy, and God restores His righteousness to that man.
Job.33.26.kjv: He shall pray unto God, and he will be favourable unto him: and he shall see his face with joy: for he will render unto man his righteousness.

Job.33.27.bsb: Then he sings before men with these words: ‘I have sinned and perverted what was right; yet I did not get what I deserved.
Job.33.27.kjv: He looketh upon men, and if any say, I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, and it profited me not;

Job.33.28.bsb: He redeemed my soul from going down to the Pit, and I will live to see the light.’
Job.33.28.kjv: He will deliver his soul from going into the pit, and his life shall see the light.

Job.33.29.bsb: Behold, all these things God does to a man, two or even three times,
Job.33.29.kjv: Lo, all these things worketh God oftentimes with man,

Job.33.30.bsb: to bring back his soul from the Pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of life.
Job.33.30.kjv: To bring back his soul from the pit, to be enlightened with the light of the living.

Job.34.10.bsb: Therefore listen to me, O men of understanding. Far be it from God to do wrong, and from the Almighty to act unjustly.
Job.34.10.kjv: Therefore hearken unto me, ye men of understanding: far be it from God, that he should do wickedness; and from the Almighty, that he should commit iniquity.

Job.34.11.bsb: For according to a man’s deeds He repays him; according to a man’s ways He brings consequences.
Job.34.11.kjv: For the work of a man shall he render unto him, and cause every man to find according to his ways.

Job.34.12.bsb: Indeed, it is true that God does not act wickedly, and the Almighty does not pervert justice.
Job.34.12.kjv: Yea, surely God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert judgment.

Job.34.13.bsb: Who gave Him charge over the earth? Who appointed Him over the whole world?
Job.34.13.kjv: Who hath given him a charge over the earth? or who hath disposed the whole world?

Job.34.21.bsb: For His eyes are on the ways of a man, and He sees his every step.
Job.34.21.kjv: For his eyes are upon the ways of man, and he seeth all his goings.

Job.34.22.bsb: There is no darkness or deep shadow where the workers of iniquity can hide.
Job.34.22.kjv: There is no darkness, nor shadow of death, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.

Job.34.23.bsb: For God need not examine a man further or have him approach for judgment.
Job.34.23.kjv: For he will not lay upon man more than right; that he should enter into judgment with God.

Job.34.24.bsb: He shatters the mighty without inquiry and sets up others in their place.
Job.34.24.kjv: He shall break in pieces mighty men without number, and set others in their stead.

Job.34.25.bsb: Therefore, He recognizes their deeds; He overthrows them in the night and they are crushed.
Job.34.25.kjv: Therefore he knoweth their works, and he overturneth them in the night, so that they are destroyed.

Job.34.28.bsb: They caused the cry of the poor to come before Him, and He heard the outcry of the afflicted.
Job.34.28.kjv: So that they cause the cry of the poor to come unto him, and he heareth the cry of the afflicted.

Job.34.29.bsb: But when He remains silent, who can condemn Him? When He hides His face, who can see Him? Yet He watches over both man and nation,
Job.34.29.kjv: When he giveth quietness, who then can make trouble? and when he hideth his face, who then can behold him? whether it be done against a nation, or against a man only:

Job.34.30.bsb: that godless men should not rule or lay snares for the people.
Job.34.30.kjv: That the hypocrite reign not, lest the people be ensnared.

Job.37.1.bsb: “At this my heart also pounds and leaps from its place.
Job.37.1.kjv: At this also my heart trembleth, and is moved out of his place.

Job.37.2.bsb: Listen closely to the thunder of His voice and the rumbling that comes from His mouth.
Job.37.2.kjv: Hear attentively the noise of his voice, and the sound that goeth out of his mouth.

Job.37.3.bsb: He unleashes His lightning beneath the whole sky and sends it to the ends of the earth.
Job.37.3.kjv: He directeth it under the whole heaven, and his lightning unto the ends of the earth.

Job.37.4.bsb: Then there comes a roaring sound; He thunders with His majestic voice. He does not restrain the lightning when His voice resounds.
Job.37.4.kjv: After it a voice roareth: he thundereth with the voice of his excellency; and he will not stay them when his voice is heard.

Job.37.5.bsb: God thunders wondrously with His voice; He does great things we cannot comprehend.
Job.37.5.kjv: God thundereth marvellously with his voice; great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend.

Job.37.6.bsb: For He says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth,’ and to the gentle rain, ‘Pour out a mighty downpour.’
Job.37.6.kjv: For he saith to the snow, Be thou on the earth; likewise to the small rain, and to the great rain of his strength.

Job.37.7.bsb: He seals up the hand of every man, so that all men may know His work.
Job.37.7.kjv: He sealeth up the hand of every man; that all men may know his work.

Job.37.8.bsb: The wild animals enter their lairs; they settle down in their dens.
Job.37.8.kjv: Then the beasts go into dens, and remain in their places.

Job.37.9.bsb: The tempest comes from its chamber, and the cold from the driving north winds.
Job.37.9.kjv: Out of the south cometh the whirlwind: and cold out of the north.

Job.37.10.bsb: By the breath of God the ice is formed and the watery expanses are frozen.
Job.37.10.kjv: By the breath of God frost is given: and the breadth of the waters is straitened.

Job.37.11.bsb: He loads the clouds with moisture; He scatters His lightning through them.
Job.37.11.kjv: Also by watering he wearieth the thick cloud: he scattereth his bright cloud:

Job.37.12.bsb: They swirl about, whirling at His direction, accomplishing all that He commands over the face of all the earth.
Job.37.12.kjv: And it is turned round about by his counsels: that they may do whatsoever he commandeth them upon the face of the world in the earth.

Job.37.13.bsb: Whether for punishment or for His land, He accomplishes this in His loving devotion.
Job.37.13.kjv: He causeth it to come, whether for correction, or for his land, or for mercy.

Job.37.14.bsb: Listen to this, O Job; stand still and consider the wonders of God.
Job.37.14.kjv: Hearken unto this, O Job: stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.

Job.37.15.bsb: Do you know how God dispatches the clouds or makes the lightning flash?
Job.37.15.kjv: Dost thou know when God disposed them, and caused the light of his cloud to shine?

Job.37.16.bsb: Do you understand how the clouds float, those wonders of Him who is perfect in knowledge?
Job.37.16.kjv: Dost thou know the balancings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him which is perfect in knowledge?

Job.37.17.bsb: You whose clothes get hot when the land lies hushed under the south wind,
Job.37.17.kjv: How thy garments are warm, when he quieteth the earth by the south wind?

Job.37.18.bsb: can you, like Him, spread out the skies, as strong as a mirror of bronze?
Job.37.18.kjv: Hast thou with him spread out the sky, which is strong, and as a molten looking glass?

Job.37.19.bsb: Teach us what we should say to Him; we cannot draw up our case because of our darkness.
Job.37.19.kjv: Teach us what we shall say unto him; for we cannot order our speech by reason of darkness.

Job.37.21.bsb: Now no one can gaze at the sun when it is bright in the skies after the wind has swept them clean.
Job.37.21.kjv: And now men see not the bright light which is in the clouds: but the wind passeth, and cleanseth them.

Job.37.23.bsb: The Almighty is beyond our reach; He is exalted in power! In His justice and great righteousness He does not oppress.
Job.37.23.kjv: Touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out: he is excellent in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice: he will not afflict.

Job.37.24.bsb: Therefore, men fear Him, for He is not partial to the wise in heart.”
Job.37.24.kjv: Men do therefore fear him: he respecteth not any that are wise of heart.

Job.38.1.bsb: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:
Job.38.1.kjv: Then the Lord answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said,

Job.38.2.bsb: “Who is this who obscures My counsel by words without knowledge?
Job.38.2.kjv: Who is this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge?

Job.38.3.bsb: Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me.
Job.38.3.kjv: Gird up now thy loins like a man; for I will demand of thee, and answer thou me.

Job.38.4.bsb: Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell Me, if you have understanding.
Job.38.4.kjv: Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.

Job.38.5.bsb: Who fixed its measurements? Surely you know! Or who stretched a measuring line across it?
Job.38.5.kjv: Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest? or who hath stretched the line upon it?

Job.38.6.bsb: On what were its foundations set, or who laid its cornerstone,
Job.38.6.kjv: Whereupon are the foundations thereof fastened? or who laid the corner stone thereof;

Job.38.8.bsb: Who enclosed the sea behind doors when it burst forth from the womb,
Job.38.8.kjv: Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it brake forth, as if it had issued out of the womb?

Job.38.9.bsb: when I made the clouds its garment and thick darkness its blanket,
Job.38.9.kjv: When I made the cloud the garment thereof, and thick darkness a swaddlingband for it,

Job.38.10.bsb: when I fixed its boundaries and set in place its bars and doors,
Job.38.10.kjv: And brake up for it my decreed place, and set bars and doors,

Job.38.11.bsb: and I declared: ‘You may come this far, but no farther; here your proud waves must stop’?
Job.38.11.kjv: And said, Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further: and here shall thy proud waves be stayed?

Job.38.12.bsb: In your days, have you commanded the morning or assigned the dawn its place,
Job.38.12.kjv: Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days; and caused the dayspring to know his place;

Job.38.13.bsb: that it might spread to the ends of the earth and shake the wicked out of it?
Job.38.13.kjv: That it might take hold of the ends of the earth, that the wicked might be shaken out of it?

Job.38.14.bsb: The earth takes shape like clay under a seal; its hills stand out like the folds of a garment.
Job.38.14.kjv: It is turned as clay to the seal; and they stand as a garment.

Job.38.15.bsb: Light is withheld from the wicked, and their upraised arm is broken.
Job.38.15.kjv: And from the wicked their light is withholden, and the high arm shall be broken.

Job.38.16.bsb: Have you journeyed to the vents of the sea or walked in the trenches of the deep?
Job.38.16.kjv: Hast thou entered into the springs of the sea? or hast thou walked in the search of the depth?

Job.38.18.bsb: Have you surveyed the extent of the earth? Tell Me, if you know all this.
Job.38.18.kjv: Hast thou perceived the breadth of the earth? declare if thou knowest it all.

Job.38.19.bsb: Where is the way to the home of light? Do you know where darkness resides,
Job.38.19.kjv: Where is the way where light dwelleth? and as for darkness, where is the place thereof,

Job.38.20.bsb: so you can lead it back to its border? Do you know the paths to its home?
Job.38.20.kjv: That thou shouldest take it to the bound thereof, and that thou shouldest know the paths to the house thereof?

Job.38.21.bsb: Surely you know, for you were already born! And the number of your days is great!
Job.38.21.kjv: Knowest thou it, because thou wast then born? or because the number of thy days is great?

Job.38.22.bsb: Have you entered the storehouses of snow or observed the storehouses of hail,
Job.38.22.kjv: Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow? or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail,

Job.38.23.bsb: which I hold in reserve for times of trouble, for the day of war and battle?
Job.38.23.kjv: Which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war?

Job.38.24.bsb: In which direction is the lightning dispersed, or the east wind scattered over the earth?
Job.38.24.kjv: By what way is the light parted, which scattereth the east wind upon the earth?

Job.38.25.bsb: Who cuts a channel for the flood or clears a path for the thunderbolt,
Job.38.25.kjv: Who hath divided a watercourse for the overflowing of waters, or a way for the lightning of thunder;

Job.38.26.bsb: to bring rain on a barren land, on a desert where no man lives,
Job.38.26.kjv: To cause it to rain on the earth, where no man is; on the wilderness, wherein there is no man;

Job.38.27.bsb: to satisfy the parched wasteland and make it sprout with tender grass?
Job.38.27.kjv: To satisfy the desolate and waste ground; and to cause the bud of the tender herb to spring forth?

Job.38.28.bsb: Does the rain have a father? Who has begotten the drops of dew?
Job.38.28.kjv: Hath the rain a father? or who hath begotten the drops of dew?

Job.38.29.bsb: From whose womb does the ice emerge? Who gives birth to the frost from heaven,
Job.38.29.kjv: Out of whose womb came the ice? and the hoary frost of heaven, who hath gendered it?

Job.38.30.bsb: when the waters become hard as stone and the surface of the deep is frozen?
Job.38.30.kjv: The waters are hid as with a stone, and the face of the deep is frozen.

Job.38.31.bsb: Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades or loosen the belt of Orion?
Job.38.31.kjv: Canst thou bind the sweet influences of Pleiades, or loose the bands of Orion?

Job.38.32.bsb: Can you bring forth the constellations in their seasons or lead out the Bear and her cubs?
Job.38.32.kjv: Canst thou bring forth Mazzaroth in his season? or canst thou guide Arcturus with his sons?

Job.38.33.bsb: Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you set their dominion over the earth?
Job.38.33.kjv: Knowest thou the ordinances of heaven? canst thou set the dominion thereof in the earth?

Job.38.34.bsb: Can you command the clouds so that a flood of water covers you?
Job.38.34.kjv: Canst thou lift up thy voice to the clouds, that abundance of waters may cover thee?

Job.38.35.bsb: Can you send the lightning bolts on their way? Do they report to you, ‘Here we are’?
Job.38.35.kjv: Canst thou send lightnings, that they may go, and say unto thee, Here we are?

Job.38.36.bsb: Who has put wisdom in the heart or given understanding to the mind?
Job.38.36.kjv: Who hath put wisdom in the inward parts? or who hath given understanding to the heart?

Job.38.37.bsb: Who has the wisdom to count the clouds? Or who can tilt the water jars of the heavens
Job.38.37.kjv: Who can number the clouds in wisdom? or who can stay the bottles of heaven,

Job.38.38.bsb: when the dust hardens into a mass and the clods of earth stick together?
Job.38.38.kjv: When the dust groweth into hardness, and the clods cleave fast together?

Job.38.39.bsb: Can you hunt the prey for a lioness or satisfy the hunger of young lions
Job.38.39.kjv: Wilt thou hunt the prey for the lion? or fill the appetite of the young lions,

Job.38.40.bsb: when they crouch in their dens and lie in wait in the thicket?
Job.38.40.kjv: When they couch in their dens, and abide in the covert to lie in wait?

Job.38.41.bsb: Who provides food for the raven when its young cry out to God as they wander about for lack of food?
Job.38.41.kjv: Who provideth for the raven his food? when his young ones cry unto God, they wander for lack of meat.

Job.39.1.bsb: “Do you know when mountain goats give birth? Have you watched the doe bear her fawn?
