Job.39.1.kjv: Knowest thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth? or canst thou mark when the hinds do calve?

Job.39.2.bsb: Can you count the months they are pregnant? Do you know the time they give birth?
Job.39.2.kjv: Canst thou number the months that they fulfil? or knowest thou the time when they bring forth?

Job.39.3.bsb: They crouch down and bring forth their young; they deliver their newborn.
Job.39.3.kjv: They bow themselves, they bring forth their young ones, they cast out their sorrows.

Job.39.4.bsb: Their young ones thrive and grow up in the open field; they leave and do not return.
Job.39.4.kjv: Their young ones are in good liking, they grow up with corn; they go forth, and return not unto them.

Job.39.5.bsb: Who set the wild donkey free? Who released the swift donkey from the harness?
Job.39.5.kjv: Who hath sent out the wild ass free? or who hath loosed the bands of the wild ass?

Job.39.6.bsb: I made the wilderness his home and the salt flats his dwelling.
Job.39.6.kjv: Whose house I have made the wilderness, and the barren land his dwellings.

Job.39.7.bsb: He scorns the tumult of the city and never hears the shouts of a driver.
Job.39.7.kjv: He scorneth the multitude of the city, neither regardeth he the crying of the driver.

Job.39.8.bsb: He roams the mountains for pasture, searching for any green thing.
Job.39.8.kjv: The range of the mountains is his pasture, and he searcheth after every green thing.

Job.39.9.bsb: Will the wild ox consent to serve you? Will he stay by your manger at night?
Job.39.9.kjv: Will the unicorn be willing to serve thee, or abide by thy crib?

Job.39.10.bsb: Can you hold him to the furrow with a harness? Will he plow the valleys behind you?
Job.39.10.kjv: Canst thou bind the unicorn with his band in the furrow? or will he harrow the valleys after thee?

Job.39.11.bsb: Can you rely on his great strength? Will you leave your hard work to him?
Job.39.11.kjv: Wilt thou trust him, because his strength is great? or wilt thou leave thy labour to him?

Job.39.12.bsb: Can you trust him to bring in your grain and gather it to your threshing floor?
Job.39.12.kjv: Wilt thou believe him, that he will bring home thy seed, and gather it into thy barn?

Job.39.13.bsb: The wings of the ostrich flap joyfully, but cannot match the pinions and feathers of the stork.
Job.39.13.kjv: Gavest thou the goodly wings unto the peacocks? or wings and feathers unto the ostrich?

Job.39.14.bsb: For she leaves her eggs on the ground and lets them warm in the sand.
Job.39.14.kjv: Which leaveth her eggs in the earth, and warmeth them in dust,

Job.39.15.bsb: She forgets that a foot may crush them, or a wild animal may trample them.
Job.39.15.kjv: And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, or that the wild beast may break them.

Job.39.16.bsb: She treats her young harshly, as if not her own, with no concern that her labor was in vain.
Job.39.16.kjv: She is hardened against her young ones, as though they were not hers: her labour is in vain without fear;

Job.39.17.bsb: For God has deprived her of wisdom; He has not endowed her with understanding.
Job.39.17.kjv: Because God hath deprived her of wisdom, neither hath he imparted to her understanding.

Job.39.18.bsb: Yet when she proudly spreads her wings, she laughs at the horse and its rider.
Job.39.18.kjv: What time she lifteth up herself on high, she scorneth the horse and his rider.

Job.39.19.bsb: Do you give strength to the horse or adorn his neck with a mane?
Job.39.19.kjv: Hast thou given the horse strength? hast thou clothed his neck with thunder?

Job.39.20.bsb: Do you make him leap like a locust, striking terror with his proud snorting?
Job.39.20.kjv: Canst thou make him afraid as a grasshopper? the glory of his nostrils is terrible.

Job.39.21.bsb: He paws in the valley and rejoices in his strength; he charges into battle.
Job.39.21.kjv: He paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in his strength: he goeth on to meet the armed men.

Job.39.22.bsb: He laughs at fear, frightened of nothing; he does not turn back from the sword.
Job.39.22.kjv: He mocketh at fear, and is not affrighted; neither turneth he back from the sword.

Job.39.23.bsb: A quiver rattles at his side, along with a flashing spear and lance.
Job.39.23.kjv: The quiver rattleth against him, the glittering spear and the shield.

Job.39.24.bsb: Trembling with excitement, he devours the distance; he cannot stand still when the ram’s horn sounds.
Job.39.24.kjv: He swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage: neither believeth he that it is the sound of the trumpet.

Job.39.25.bsb: At the blast of the horn, he snorts with fervor. He catches the scent of battle from afar, the shouts of captains and the cry of war.
Job.39.25.kjv: He saith among the trumpets, Ha, ha; and he smelleth the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.

Job.39.26.bsb: Does the hawk take flight by your understanding and spread his wings toward the south?
Job.39.26.kjv: Doth the hawk fly by thy wisdom, and stretch her wings toward the south?

Job.39.27.bsb: Does the eagle soar at your command and make his nest on high?
Job.39.27.kjv: Doth the eagle mount up at thy command, and make her nest on high?

Job.39.28.bsb: He dwells on a cliff and lodges there; his stronghold is on a rocky crag.
Job.39.28.kjv: She dwelleth and abideth on the rock, upon the crag of the rock, and the strong place.

Job.39.29.bsb: From there he spies out food; his eyes see it from afar.
Job.39.29.kjv: From thence she seeketh the prey, and her eyes behold afar off.

Job.39.30.bsb: His young ones feast on blood; and where the slain are, there he is.”
Job.39.30.kjv: Her young ones also suck up blood: and where the slain are, there is she.

Job.40.1.bsb: And the LORD said to Job:
Job.40.1.kjv: Moreover the Lord answered Job, and said,

Job.40.3.kjv: Then Job answered the Lord, and said,

Job.40.4.bsb: “Behold, I am insignificant. How can I reply to You? I place my hand over my mouth.
Job.40.4.kjv: Behold, I am vile; what shall I answer thee? I will lay mine hand upon my mouth.

Job.40.5.bsb: I have spoken once, but I have no answer—twice, but I have nothing to add.”
Job.40.5.kjv: Once have I spoken; but I will not answer: yea, twice; but I will proceed no further.

Job.40.6.bsb: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:
Job.40.6.kjv: Then answered the Lord unto Job out of the whirlwind, and said,

Job.40.7.bsb: “Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me.
Job.40.7.kjv: Gird up thy loins now like a man: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.

Job.40.8.bsb: Would you really annul My justice? Would you condemn Me to justify yourself?
Job.40.8.kjv: Wilt thou also disannul my judgment? wilt thou condemn me, that thou mayest be righteous?

Job.40.9.bsb: Do you have an arm like God’s? Can you thunder with a voice like His?
Job.40.9.kjv: Hast thou an arm like God? or canst thou thunder with a voice like him?

Job.40.10.bsb: Then adorn yourself with majesty and splendor, and clothe yourself with honor and glory.
Job.40.10.kjv: Deck thyself now with majesty and excellency; and array thyself with glory and beauty.

Job.40.11.bsb: Unleash the fury of your wrath; look on every proud man and bring him low.
Job.40.11.kjv: Cast abroad the rage of thy wrath: and behold every one that is proud, and abase him.

Job.40.12.bsb: Look on every proud man and humble him; trample the wicked where they stand.
Job.40.12.kjv: Look on every one that is proud, and bring him low; and tread down the wicked in their place.

Job.40.13.bsb: Bury them together in the dust; imprison them in the grave.
Job.40.13.kjv: Hide them in the dust together; and bind their faces in secret.

Job.40.14.bsb: Then I will confess to you that your own right hand can save you.
Job.40.14.kjv: Then will I also confess unto thee that thine own right hand can save thee.

Job.40.15.bsb: Look at Behemoth, which I made along with you. He feeds on grass like an ox.
Job.40.15.kjv: Behold now behemoth, which I made with thee; he eateth grass as an ox.

Job.40.16.bsb: See the strength of his loins and the power in the muscles of his belly.
Job.40.16.kjv: Lo now, his strength is in his loins, and his force is in the navel of his belly.

Job.40.17.bsb: His tail sways like a cedar; the sinews of his thighs are tightly knit.
Job.40.17.kjv: He moveth his tail like a cedar: the sinews of his stones are wrapped together.

Job.40.18.bsb: His bones are tubes of bronze; his limbs are rods of iron.
Job.40.18.kjv: His bones are as strong pieces of brass; his bones are like bars of iron.

Job.40.19.bsb: He is the foremost of God’s works; only his Maker can draw the sword against him.
Job.40.19.kjv: He is the chief of the ways of God: he that made him can make his sword to approach unto him.

Job.40.20.bsb: The hills yield him their produce, while all the beasts of the field play nearby.
Job.40.20.kjv: Surely the mountains bring him forth food, where all the beasts of the field play.

Job.40.21.bsb: He lies under the lotus plants, hidden among the reeds of the marsh.
Job.40.21.kjv: He lieth under the shady trees, in the covert of the reed, and fens.

Job.40.22.bsb: The lotus plants conceal him in their shade; the willows of the brook surround him.
Job.40.22.kjv: The shady trees cover him with their shadow; the willows of the brook compass him about.

Job.40.23.bsb: Though the river rages, Behemoth is unafraid; he remains secure, though the Jordan surges to his mouth.
Job.40.23.kjv: Behold, he drinketh up a river, and hasteth not: he trusteth that he can draw up Jordan into his mouth.

Job.40.24.bsb: Can anyone capture him as he looks on, or pierce his nose with a snare?
Job.40.24.kjv: He taketh it with his eyes: his nose pierceth through snares.

Job.41.1.bsb: “Can you pull in Leviathan with a hook or tie down his tongue with a rope?
Job.41.1.kjv: Canst thou draw out leviathan with an hook? or his tongue with a cord which thou lettest down?

Job.41.2.bsb: Can you put a cord through his nose or pierce his jaw with a hook?
Job.41.2.kjv: Canst thou put an hook into his nose? or bore his jaw through with a thorn?

Job.41.3.bsb: Will he beg you for mercy or speak to you softly?
Job.41.3.kjv: Will he make many supplications unto thee? will he speak soft words unto thee?

Job.41.4.bsb: Will he make a covenant with you to take him as a slave for life?
Job.41.4.kjv: Will he make a covenant with thee? wilt thou take him for a servant for ever?

Job.41.5.bsb: Can you pet him like a bird or put him on a leash for your maidens?
Job.41.5.kjv: Wilt thou play with him as with a bird? or wilt thou bind him for thy maidens?

Job.41.6.bsb: Will traders barter for him or divide him among the merchants?
Job.41.6.kjv: Shall the companions make a banquet of him? shall they part him among the merchants?

Job.41.7.bsb: Can you fill his hide with harpoons or his head with fishing spears?
Job.41.7.kjv: Canst thou fill his skin with barbed irons? or his head with fish spears?

Job.41.8.bsb: If you lay a hand on him, you will remember the battle and never repeat it!
Job.41.8.kjv: Lay thine hand upon him, remember the battle, do no more.

Job.41.9.bsb: Surely hope of overcoming him is false. Is not the sight of him overwhelming?
Job.41.9.kjv: Behold, the hope of him is in vain: shall not one be cast down even at the sight of him?

Job.41.10.bsb: No one is so fierce as to rouse Leviathan. Then who is able to stand against Me?
Job.41.10.kjv: None is so fierce that dare stir him up: who then is able to stand before me?

Job.41.11.bsb: Who has given to Me that I should repay him? Everything under heaven is Mine.
Job.41.11.kjv: Who hath prevented me, that I should repay him? whatsoever is under the whole heaven is mine.

Job.41.12.bsb: I cannot keep silent about his limbs, his power and graceful form.
Job.41.12.kjv: I will not conceal his parts, nor his power, nor his comely proportion.

Job.41.13.bsb: Who can strip off his outer coat? Who can approach him with a bridle?
Job.41.13.kjv: Who can discover the face of his garment? or who can come to him with his double bridle?

Job.41.14.bsb: Who can open his jaws, ringed by his fearsome teeth?
Job.41.14.kjv: Who can open the doors of his face? his teeth are terrible round about.

Job.41.15.bsb: His rows of scales are his pride, tightly sealed together.
Job.41.15.kjv: His scales are his pride, shut up together as with a close seal.

Job.41.16.bsb: One scale is so near to another that no air can pass between them.
Job.41.16.kjv: One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.

Job.41.17.bsb: They are joined to one another; they clasp and cannot be separated.
Job.41.17.kjv: They are joined one to another, they stick together, that they cannot be sundered.

Job.41.18.bsb: His snorting flashes with light, and his eyes are like the rays of dawn.
Job.41.18.kjv: By his neesings a light doth shine, and his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.

Job.41.19.bsb: Firebrands stream from his mouth; fiery sparks shoot forth!
Job.41.19.kjv: Out of his mouth go burning lamps, and sparks of fire leap out.

Job.41.20.bsb: Smoke billows from his nostrils as from a boiling pot over burning reeds.
Job.41.20.kjv: Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, as out of a seething pot or caldron.

Job.41.21.bsb: His breath sets coals ablaze, and flames pour from his mouth.
Job.41.21.kjv: His breath kindleth coals, and a flame goeth out of his mouth.

Job.41.22.bsb: Strength resides in his neck, and dismay leaps before him.
Job.41.22.kjv: In his neck remaineth strength, and sorrow is turned into joy before him.

Job.41.23.bsb: The folds of his flesh are tightly joined; they are firm and immovable.
Job.41.23.kjv: The flakes of his flesh are joined together: they are firm in themselves; they cannot be moved.

Job.41.24.bsb: His chest is as hard as a rock, as hard as a lower millstone!
Job.41.24.kjv: His heart is as firm as a stone; yea, as hard as a piece of the nether millstone.

Job.41.25.bsb: When Leviathan rises up, the mighty are terrified; they withdraw before his thrashing.
Job.41.25.kjv: When he raiseth up himself, the mighty are afraid: by reason of breakings they purify themselves.

Job.41.26.bsb: The sword that reaches him has no effect, nor does the spear or dart or arrow.
Job.41.26.kjv: The sword of him that layeth at him cannot hold: the spear, the dart, nor the habergeon.

Job.41.27.bsb: He regards iron as straw and bronze as rotten wood.
Job.41.27.kjv: He esteemeth iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood.

Job.41.28.bsb: No arrow can make him flee; slingstones become like chaff to him.
Job.41.28.kjv: The arrow cannot make him flee: slingstones are turned with him into stubble.

Job.41.29.bsb: A club is regarded as straw, and he laughs at the sound of the lance.
Job.41.29.kjv: Darts are counted as stubble: he laugheth at the shaking of a spear.

Job.41.30.bsb: His undersides are jagged potsherds, spreading out the mud like a threshing sledge.
Job.41.30.kjv: Sharp stones are under him: he spreadeth sharp pointed things upon the mire.

Job.41.31.bsb: He makes the depths seethe like a cauldron; he makes the sea like a jar of ointment.
Job.41.31.kjv: He maketh the deep to boil like a pot: he maketh the sea like a pot of ointment.

Job.41.32.bsb: He leaves a glistening wake behind him; one would think the deep had white hair!
Job.41.32.kjv: He maketh a path to shine after him; one would think the deep to be hoary.

Job.41.33.bsb: Nothing on earth is his equal—a creature devoid of fear!
Job.41.33.kjv: Upon earth there is not his like, who is made without fear.

Job.41.34.bsb: He looks down on all the haughty; he is king over all the proud.”
Job.41.34.kjv: He beholdeth all high things: he is a king over all the children of pride.

Job.42.1.bsb: Then Job replied to the LORD:
Job.42.1.kjv: Then Job answered the Lord, and said,

Job.42.3.bsb: You asked, ‘Who is this who conceals My counsel without knowledge?’ Surely I spoke of things I did not understand, things too wonderful for me to know.
Job.42.3.kjv: Who is he that hideth counsel without knowledge? therefore have I uttered that I understood not; things too wonderful for me, which I knew not.

Job.42.4.bsb: You said, ‘Listen now, and I will speak. I will question you, and you shall inform Me.’
Job.42.4.kjv: Hear, I beseech thee, and I will speak: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.

Job.42.5.bsb: My ears had heard of You, but now my eyes have seen You.
Job.42.5.kjv: I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee.

Job.42.6.bsb: Therefore I despise myself, and I repent in dust and ashes.”
Job.42.6.kjv: Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.

Job.28.23.bsb: But God understands its way, and He knows its place.
Job.28.23.kjv: God understandeth the way thereof, and he knoweth the place thereof.

Job.28.24.bsb: For He looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under the heavens.
Job.28.24.kjv: For he looketh to the ends of the earth, and seeth under the whole heaven;

Job.28.25.bsb: When God fixed the weight of the wind and measured out the waters,
Job.28.25.kjv: To make the weight for the winds; and he weigheth the waters by measure.

Job.28.26.bsb: when He set a limit for the rain and a path for the thunderbolt,
Job.28.26.kjv: When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder:

Job.27.3.bsb: as long as my breath is still within me and the breath of God remains in my nostrils,
Job.27.3.kjv: All the while my breath is in me, and the spirit of God is in my nostrils;

Job.36.26.bsb: Indeed, God is great—beyond our knowledge; the number of His years is unsearchable.
Job.36.26.kjv: Behold, God is great, and we know him not, neither can the number of his years be searched out.

Job.13.11.bsb: Would His majesty not terrify you? Would the dread of Him not fall upon you?
Job.13.11.kjv: Shall not his excellency make you afraid? and his dread fall upon you?

Job.35.5.bsb: Look to the heavens and see; gaze at the clouds high above you.
Job.35.5.kjv: Look unto the heavens, and see; and behold the clouds which are higher than thou.

Job.35.6.bsb: If you sin, what do you accomplish against Him? If you multiply your transgressions, what do you do to Him?
Job.35.6.kjv: If thou sinnest, what doest thou against him? or if thy transgressions be multiplied, what doest thou unto him?

Job.35.7.bsb: If you are righteous, what do you give Him, or what does He receive from your hand?
Job.35.7.kjv: If thou be righteous, what givest thou him? or what receiveth he of thine hand?

Job.29.3.bsb: when His lamp shone above my head, and by His light I walked through the darkness,
Job.29.3.kjv: When his candle shined upon my head, and when by his light I walked through darkness;

Job.29.5.bsb: when the Almighty was still with me and my children were around me,
Job.29.5.kjv: When the Almighty was yet with me, when my children were about me;

Job.36.23.bsb: Who has appointed His way for Him, or told Him, ‘You have done wrong’?
Job.36.23.kjv: Who hath enjoined him his way? or who can say, Thou hast wrought iniquity?

Job.23.13.bsb: But He is unchangeable, and who can oppose Him? He does what He desires.
Job.23.13.kjv: But he is in one mind, and who can turn him? and what his soul desireth, even that he doeth.

Job.36.5.bsb: Indeed, God is mighty, but He despises no one; He is mighty in strength of understanding.
Job.36.5.kjv: Behold, God is mighty, and despiseth not any: he is mighty in strength and wisdom.

Job.11.7.bsb: Can you fathom the deep things of God or discover the limits of the Almighty?
Job.11.7.kjv: Canst thou by searching find out God? canst thou find out the Almighty unto perfection?

Job.11.8.bsb: They are higher than the heavens—what can you do? They are deeper than Sheol—what can you know?
Job.11.8.kjv: It is as high as heaven; what canst thou do? deeper than hell; what canst thou know?

Job.11.9.bsb: Their measure is longer than the earth and wider than the sea.
Job.11.9.kjv: The measure thereof is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.

Job.15.8.bsb: Do you listen in on the council of God or limit wisdom to yourself?
Job.15.8.kjv: Hast thou heard the secret of God? and dost thou restrain wisdom to thyself?

Job.23.8.bsb: If I go east, He is not there, and if I go west, I cannot find Him.
Job.23.8.kjv: Behold, I go forward, but he is not there; and backward, but I cannot perceive him:

Job.23.9.bsb: When He is at work in the north, I cannot behold Him; when He turns to the south, I cannot see Him.
Job.23.9.kjv: On the left hand, where he doth work, but I cannot behold him: he hideth himself on the right hand, that I cannot see him:

Job.8.3.bsb: Does God pervert justice? Does the Almighty pervert what is right?
Job.8.3.kjv: Doth God pervert judgment? or doth the Almighty pervert justice?

Job.21.22.bsb: Can anyone teach knowledge to God, since He judges those on high?
Job.21.22.kjv: Shall any teach God knowledge? seeing he judgeth those that are high.

Job.23.7.bsb: Then an upright man could reason with Him, and I would be delivered forever from my Judge.
Job.23.7.kjv: There the righteous might dispute with him; so should I be delivered for ever from my judge.

Job.31.13.bsb: If I have rejected the cause of my manservant or maidservant when they made a complaint against me,
Job.31.13.kjv: If I did despise the cause of my manservant or of my maidservant, when they contended with me;

Job.31.14.bsb: what will I do when God rises to judge? How will I answer when called to account?
Job.31.14.kjv: What then shall I do when God riseth up? and when he visiteth, what shall I answer him?

Job.36.3.bsb: I get my knowledge from afar, and I will ascribe justice to my Maker.
Job.36.3.kjv: I will fetch my knowledge from afar, and will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.

Job.11.11.bsb: Surely He knows the deceit of men. If He sees iniquity, does He not take note?
Job.11.11.kjv: For he knoweth vain men: he seeth wickedness also; will he not then consider it?

Job.12.22.bsb: He reveals the deep things of darkness and brings deep shadows into light.
Job.12.22.kjv: He discovereth deep things out of darkness, and bringeth out to light the shadow of death.

Job.23.10.bsb: Yet He knows the way I have taken; when He has tested me, I will come forth as gold.
Job.23.10.kjv: But he knoweth the way that I take: when he hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold.

Job.24.1.bsb: “Why does the Almighty not reserve times for judgment? Why may those who know Him never see His days?
Job.24.1.kjv: Why, seeing times are not hidden from the Almighty, do they that know him not see his days?

Job.24.23.bsb: He gives them a sense of security, but His eyes are on their ways.
Job.24.23.kjv: Though it be given him to be in safety, whereon he resteth; yet his eyes are upon their ways.

Job.26.6.bsb: Sheol is naked before God, and Abaddon has no covering.
Job.26.6.kjv: Hell is naked before him, and destruction hath no covering.

Job.28.10.bsb: He hews out channels in the rocks, and his eyes spot every treasure.
Job.28.10.kjv: He cutteth out rivers among the rocks; and his eye seeth every precious thing.

Job.31.4.bsb: Does He not see my ways and count my every step?
Job.31.4.kjv: Doth not he see my ways, and count all my steps?

Job.36.4.bsb: For truly my words are free of falsehood; one perfect in knowledge is with you.
Job.36.4.kjv: For truly my words shall not be false: he that is perfect in knowledge is with thee.

Job.11.6.bsb: and disclose to you the secrets of wisdom, for true wisdom has two sides. Know then that God exacts from you less than your iniquity deserves.
Job.11.6.kjv: And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is! Know therefore that God exacteth of thee less than thine iniquity deserveth.

Job.23.2.bsb: “Even today my complaint is bitter. His hand is heavy despite my groaning.
Job.23.2.kjv: Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning.

Job.23.3.bsb: If only I knew where to find Him, so that I could go to His seat.
Job.23.3.kjv: Oh that I knew where I might find him! that I might come even to his seat!

Job.23.4.bsb: I would plead my case before Him and fill my mouth with arguments.
Job.23.4.kjv: I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments.

Job.23.5.bsb: I would learn how He would answer, and consider what He would say.
Job.23.5.kjv: I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me.

Job.24.12.bsb: From the city, men groan, and the souls of the wounded cry out, yet God charges no one with wrongdoing.
Job.24.12.kjv: Men groan from out of the city, and the soul of the wounded crieth out: yet God layeth not folly to them.

Job.11.10.bsb: If He comes along to imprison you, or convenes a court, who can stop Him?
Job.11.10.kjv: If he cut off, and shut up, or gather together, then who can hinder him?

Job.23.14.bsb: For He carries out His decree against me, and He has many such plans.
Job.23.14.kjv: For he performeth the thing that is appointed for me: and many such things are with him.

Job.36.22.bsb: Behold, God is exalted in His power. Who is a teacher like Him?
Job.36.22.kjv: Behold, God exalteth by his power: who teacheth like him?

Job.36.27.bsb: For He draws up drops of water which distill the rain from the mist,
Job.36.27.kjv: For he maketh small the drops of water: they pour down rain according to the vapour thereof:

Job.36.28.bsb: which the clouds pour out and shower abundantly on mankind.
Job.36.28.kjv: Which the clouds do drop and distil upon man abundantly.

Job.36.29.bsb: Furthermore, who can understand how the clouds spread out, how the thunder roars from His pavilion?
Job.36.29.kjv: Also can any understand the spreadings of the clouds, or the noise of his tabernacle?

Job.36.30.bsb: See how He scatters His lightning around Him and covers the depths of the sea.
Job.36.30.kjv: Behold, he spreadeth his light upon it, and covereth the bottom of the sea.

Job.36.31.bsb: For by these He judges the nations and provides food in abundance.
Job.36.31.kjv: For by them judgeth he the people; he giveth meat in abundance.

Job.36.32.bsb: He fills His hands with lightning and commands it to strike its mark.
Job.36.32.kjv: With clouds he covereth the light; and commandeth it not to shine by the cloud that cometh betwixt.

Job.36.33.bsb: The thunder declares His presence; even the cattle regard the rising storm.
Job.36.33.kjv: The noise thereof sheweth concerning it, the cattle also concerning the vapour.

Job.1.10.bsb: Have You not placed a hedge on every side around him and his household and all that he owns? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his possessions have increased in the land.
Job.1.10.kjv: Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side? thou hast blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.

Job.11.18.bsb: You will be secure, because there is hope, and you will look around and lie down in safety.
Job.11.18.kjv: And thou shalt be secure, because there is hope; yea, thou shalt dig about thee, and thou shalt take thy rest in safety.

Job.11.19.bsb: You will lie down without fear, and many will court your favor.
Job.11.19.kjv: Also thou shalt lie down, and none shall make thee afraid; yea, many shall make suit unto thee.

Job.27.4.bsb: my lips will not speak wickedness, and my tongue will not utter deceit.
Job.27.4.kjv: My lips shall not speak wickedness, nor my tongue utter deceit.

Job.36.7.bsb: He does not take His eyes off the righteous, but He enthrones them with kings and exalts them forever.
Job.36.7.kjv: He withdraweth not his eyes from the righteous: but with kings are they on the throne; yea, he doth establish them for ever, and they are exalted.

Job.36.16.bsb: Indeed, He drew you from the jaws of distress to a spacious and broad place, to a table full of richness.
Job.36.16.kjv: Even so would he have removed thee out of the strait into a broad place, where there is no straitness; and that which should be set on thy table should be full of fatness.

Job.1.9.bsb: Satan answered the LORD, “Does Job fear God for nothing?
Job.1.9.kjv: Then Satan answered the Lord, and said, Doth Job fear God for nought?

Job.1.11.bsb: But stretch out Your hand and strike all that he has, and he will surely curse You to Your face.”
Job.1.11.kjv: But put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.

Job.1.12.bsb: “Very well,” said the LORD to Satan. “Everything he has is in your hands, but you must not lay a hand on the man himself.” Then Satan went out from the presence of the LORD.
Job.1.12.kjv: And the Lord said unto Satan, Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand. So Satan went forth from the presence of the Lord.

Job.2.6.bsb: “Very well,” said the LORD to Satan. “He is in your hands, but you must spare his life.”
Job.2.6.kjv: And the Lord said unto Satan, Behold, he is in thine hand; but save his life.

Job.8.6.bsb: if you are pure and upright, even now He will rouse Himself on your behalf and restore your righteous estate.
Job.8.6.kjv: If thou wert pure and upright; surely now he would awake for thee, and make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous.

Job.8.7.bsb: Though your beginnings were modest, your latter days will flourish.
Job.8.7.kjv: Though thy beginning was small, yet thy latter end should greatly increase.

Job.8.20.bsb: Behold, God does not reject the blameless, nor will He strengthen the hand of evildoers.
Job.8.20.kjv: Behold, God will not cast away a perfect man, neither will he help the evil doers:

Job.8.21.bsb: He will yet fill your mouth with laughter, and your lips with a shout of joy.
Job.8.21.kjv: Till he fill thy mouth with laughing, and thy lips with rejoicing.

Job.11.17.bsb: Your life will be brighter than noonday; its darkness will be like the morning.
Job.11.17.kjv: And thine age shall be clearer than the noonday; thou shalt shine forth, thou shalt be as the morning.

Job.12.23.bsb: He makes nations great and destroys them; He enlarges nations, then disperses them.
Job.12.23.kjv: He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them: he enlargeth the nations, and straiteneth them again.

Job.22.18.bsb: But it was He who filled their houses with good things; so I stay far from the counsel of the wicked.
Job.22.18.kjv: Yet he filled their houses with good things: but the counsel of the wicked is far from me.

Job.29.19.bsb: My roots will spread out to the waters, and the dew will rest nightly on my branches.
Job.29.19.kjv: My root was spread out by the waters, and the dew lay all night upon my branch.

Job.29.20.bsb: My glory is ever new within me, and my bow is renewed in my hand.’
Job.29.20.kjv: My glory was fresh in me, and my bow was renewed in my hand.

Job.36.11.bsb: If they obey and serve Him, then they end their days in prosperity and their years in happiness.
Job.36.11.kjv: If they obey and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.

Job.42.12.bsb: So the LORD blessed Job’s latter days more than his first. He owned 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 yoke of oxen, and 1,000 female donkeys.
Job.42.12.kjv: So the Lord blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning: for he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.

Job.12.6.bsb: The tents of robbers are safe, and those who provoke God are secure—those who carry their god in their hands.
Job.12.6.kjv: The tabernacles of robbers prosper, and they that provoke God are secure; into whose hand God bringeth abundantly.

Job.21.7.bsb: Why do the wicked live on, growing old and increasing in power?
Job.21.7.kjv: Wherefore do the wicked live, become old, yea, are mighty in power?

Job.24.2.bsb: Men move boundary stones; they pasture stolen flocks.
Job.24.2.kjv: Some remove the landmarks; they violently take away flocks, and feed thereof.

Job.24.3.bsb: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless and take the widow’s ox in pledge.
Job.24.3.kjv: They drive away the ass of the fatherless, they take the widow’s ox for a pledge.

Job.24.4.bsb: They push the needy off the road and force all the poor of the land into hiding.
Job.24.4.kjv: They turn the needy out of the way: the poor of the earth hide themselves together.

Job.24.5.bsb: Indeed, like wild donkeys in the desert, the poor go to work foraging for food; the wasteland is food for their children.
Job.24.5.kjv: Behold, as wild asses in the desert, go they forth to their work; rising betimes for a prey: the wilderness yieldeth food for them and for their children.

Job.24.6.bsb: They gather fodder in the fields and glean the vineyards of the wicked.
Job.24.6.kjv: They reap every one his corn in the field: and they gather the vintage of the wicked.

Job.24.7.bsb: Without clothing, they spend the night naked; they have no covering against the cold.
Job.24.7.kjv: They cause the naked to lodge without clothing, that they have no covering in the cold.

Job.24.8.bsb: Drenched by mountain rains, they huddle against the rocks for want of shelter.
Job.24.8.kjv: They are wet with the showers of the mountains, and embrace the rock for want of a shelter.

Job.24.10.bsb: Without clothing, they wander about naked. They carry the sheaves, but still go hungry.
Job.24.10.kjv: They cause him to go naked without clothing, and they take away the sheaf from the hungry;

Job.24.11.bsb: They crush olives within their walls; they tread the winepresses, but go thirsty.
Job.24.11.kjv: Which make oil within their walls, and tread their winepresses, and suffer thirst.

Job.3.20.bsb: Why is light given to the miserable, and life to the bitter of soul,
Job.3.20.kjv: Wherefore is light given to him that is in misery, and life unto the bitter in soul;

Job.3.21.bsb: who long for death that does not come, and search for it like hidden treasure,
Job.3.21.kjv: Which long for death, but it cometh not; and dig for it more than for hid treasures;

Job.3.22.bsb: who rejoice and greatly exult when they reach the grave?
Job.3.22.kjv: Which rejoice exceedingly, and are glad, when they can find the grave?

Job.3.23.bsb: Why is life given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?
Job.3.23.kjv: Why is light given to a man whose way is hid, and whom God hath hedged in?

Job.25.2.bsb: “Dominion and awe belong to God; He establishes harmony in the heights of heaven.
Job.25.2.kjv: Dominion and fear are with him, he maketh peace in his high places.

Job.34.33.bsb: Should God repay you on your own terms when you have disavowed Him? You must choose, not I; so tell me what you know.
Job.34.33.kjv: Should it be according to thy mind? he will recompense it, whether thou refuse, or whether thou choose; and not I: therefore speak what thou knowest.

Job.36.2.bsb: “Bear with me a little longer, and I will show you that there is more to be said on God’s behalf.
Job.36.2.kjv: Suffer me a little, and I will shew thee that I have yet to speak on God’s behalf.

Job.36.6.bsb: He does not keep the wicked alive, but He grants justice to the afflicted.
Job.36.6.kjv: He preserveth not the life of the wicked: but giveth right to the poor.

Job.36.8.bsb: And if men are bound with chains, caught in cords of affliction,
Job.36.8.kjv: And if they be bound in fetters, and be holden in cords of affliction;

Job.36.9.bsb: then He tells them their deeds and how arrogantly they have transgressed.
Job.36.9.kjv: Then he sheweth them their work, and their transgressions that they have exceeded.

Job.36.10.bsb: He opens their ears to correction and commands that they turn from iniquity.
Job.36.10.kjv: He openeth also their ear to discipline, and commandeth that they return from iniquity.

Job.36.13.bsb: The godless in heart harbor resentment; even when He binds them, they do not cry for help.
Job.36.13.kjv: But the hypocrites in heart heap up wrath: they cry not when he bindeth them.

Job.36.15.bsb: God rescues the afflicted by their affliction and opens their ears in oppression.
Job.36.15.kjv: He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.

Job.36.17.bsb: But now you are laden with the judgment due the wicked; judgment and justice have seized you.
Job.36.17.kjv: But thou hast fulfilled the judgment of the wicked: judgment and justice take hold on thee.

Job.36.21.bsb: Be careful not to turn to iniquity, for this you have preferred to affliction.
Job.36.21.kjv: Take heed, regard not iniquity: for this hast thou chosen rather than affliction.

Job.36.24.bsb: Remember to magnify His work, which men have praised in song.
Job.36.24.kjv: Remember that thou magnify his work, which men behold.

Job.36.25.bsb: All mankind has seen it; men behold it from afar.
Job.36.25.kjv: Every man may see it; man may behold it afar off.

Job.31.27.bsb: so that my heart was secretly enticed and my hand threw a kiss from my mouth,
Job.31.27.kjv: And my heart hath been secretly enticed, or my mouth hath kissed my hand:

Job.31.26.bsb: if I have beheld the sun in its radiance or the moon moving in splendor,
Job.31.26.kjv: If I beheld the sun when it shined, or the moon walking in brightness;

Job.31.28.bsb: this would also be an iniquity to be judged, for I would have denied God on high.
Job.31.28.kjv: This also were an iniquity to be punished by the judge: for I should have denied the God that is above.

Job.8.9.bsb: For we were born yesterday and know nothing; our days on earth are but a shadow.
Job.8.9.kjv: (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days upon earth are a shadow:)

Job.28.12.bsb: But where can wisdom be found, and where does understanding dwell?
Job.28.12.kjv: But where shall wisdom be found? and where is the place of understanding?

Job.28.13.bsb: No man can know its value, nor is it found in the land of the living.
Job.28.13.kjv: Man knoweth not the price thereof; neither is it found in the land of the living.

Job.28.20.bsb: From where, then, does wisdom come, and where does understanding dwell?
Job.28.20.kjv: Whence then cometh wisdom? and where is the place of understanding?

Job.28.21.bsb: It is hidden from the eyes of every living thing and concealed from the birds of the air.
Job.28.21.kjv: Seeing it is hid from the eyes of all living, and kept close from the fowls of the air.

Job.14.17.bsb: My transgression would be sealed in a bag, and You would cover over my iniquity.
Job.14.17.kjv: My transgression is sealed up in a bag, and thou sewest up mine iniquity.

Job.15.35.bsb: They conceive trouble and give birth to evil; their womb is pregnant with deceit.”
Job.15.35.kjv: They conceive mischief, and bring forth vanity, and their belly prepareth deceit.

Job.31.29.bsb: If I have rejoiced in my enemy’s ruin, or exulted when evil befell him—
Job.31.29.kjv: If I rejoiced at the destruction of him that hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him:

Job.31.30.bsb: I have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking for his life with a curse—
Job.31.30.kjv: Neither have I suffered my mouth to sin by wishing a curse to his soul.

Job.22.3.bsb: Does it delight the Almighty that you are righteous? Does He profit if your ways are blameless?
Job.22.3.kjv: Is it any pleasure to the Almighty, that thou art righteous? or is it gain to him, that thou makest thy ways perfect?

Job.22.4.bsb: Is it for your reverence that He rebukes you and enters into judgment against you?
Job.22.4.kjv: Will he reprove thee for fear of thee? will he enter with thee into judgment?

Job.22.5.bsb: Is not your wickedness great? Are not your iniquities endless?
Job.22.5.kjv: Is not thy wickedness great? and thine iniquities infinite?

Job.35.2.bsb: “Do you think this is just? You say, ‘I am more righteous than God.’
Job.35.2.kjv: Thinkest thou this to be right, that thou saidst, My righteousness is more than God’s?

Job.35.3.bsb: For you ask, ‘What does it profit me, and what benefit do I gain apart from sin?’
Job.35.3.kjv: For thou saidst, What advantage will it be unto thee? and, What profit shall I have, if I be cleansed from my sin?

Job.35.4.bsb: I will reply to you and to your friends as well.
Job.35.4.kjv: I will answer thee, and thy companions with thee.

Job.35.8.bsb: Your wickedness affects only a man like yourself, and your righteousness only a son of man.
Job.35.8.kjv: Thy wickedness may hurt a man as thou art; and thy righteousness may profit the son of man.

Job.2.12.bsb: When they lifted up their eyes from afar, they could barely recognize Job. They began to weep aloud, and each man tore his robe and threw dust in the air over his head.
Job.2.12.kjv: And when they lifted up their eyes afar off, and knew him not, they lifted up their voice, and wept; and they rent every one his mantle, and sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven.

Job.21.12.bsb: singing to the tambourine and lyre and making merry at the sound of the flute.
Job.21.12.kjv: They take the timbrel and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the organ.

Job.30.31.bsb: My harp is tuned to mourning and my flute to the sound of weeping.
Job.30.31.kjv: My harp also is turned to mourning, and my organ into the voice of them that weep.

Job.6.27.bsb: You would even cast lots for an orphan and barter away your friend.
Job.6.27.kjv: Yea, ye overwhelm the fatherless, and ye dig a pit for your friend.

Job.22.9.bsb: You sent widows away empty-handed, and the strength of the fatherless was crushed.
Job.22.9.kjv: Thou hast sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless have been broken.

Job.30.25.bsb: Have I not wept for those in trouble? Has my soul not grieved for the needy?
Job.30.25.kjv: Did not I weep for him that was in trouble? was not my soul grieved for the poor?

Job.31.38.bsb: if my land cries out against me and its furrows weep together,
Job.31.38.kjv: If my land cry against me, or that the furrows likewise thereof complain;

Job.31.39.bsb: if I have devoured its produce without payment or broken the spirit of its tenants,
Job.31.39.kjv: If I have eaten the fruits thereof without money, or have caused the owners thereof to lose their life:

Job.31.40.bsb: then let briers grow instead of wheat and stinkweed instead of barley.” Thus conclude the words of Job.
Job.31.40.kjv: Let thistles grow instead of wheat, and cockle instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.

Job.20.19.bsb: For he has oppressed and forsaken the poor; he has seized houses he did not build.
Job.20.19.kjv: Because he hath oppressed and hath forsaken the poor; because he hath violently taken away an house which he builded not;

Job.20.20.bsb: Because his appetite is never satisfied, he cannot escape with his treasure.
Job.20.20.kjv: Surely he shall not feel quietness in his belly, he shall not save of that which he desired.

Job.20.21.bsb: Nothing is left for him to consume; thus his prosperity will not endure.
Job.20.21.kjv: There shall none of his meat be left; therefore shall no man look for his goods.

Job.22.6.bsb: For you needlessly demanded security from your brothers and deprived the naked of their clothing.
Job.22.6.kjv: For thou hast taken a pledge from thy brother for nought, and stripped the naked of their clothing.

Job.22.7.bsb: You gave no water to the weary and withheld food from the famished,
Job.22.7.kjv: Thou hast not given water to the weary to drink, and thou hast withholden bread from the hungry.

Job.22.10.bsb: Therefore snares surround you, and sudden peril terrifies you;
Job.22.10.kjv: Therefore snares are round about thee, and sudden fear troubleth thee;

Job.22.11.bsb: it is so dark you cannot see, and a flood of water covers you.
Job.22.11.kjv: Or darkness, that thou canst not see; and abundance of waters cover thee.

Job.21.15.bsb: Who is the Almighty, that we should serve Him, and what would we gain if we pray to Him?’
Job.21.15.kjv: What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? and what profit should we have, if we pray unto him?

Job.30.20.bsb: I cry out to You for help, but You do not answer; when I stand up, You merely look at me.
Job.30.20.kjv: I cry unto thee, and thou dost not hear me: I stand up, and thou regardest me not.

Job.3.1.bsb: After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth.
Job.3.1.kjv: After this opened Job his mouth, and cursed his day.

Job.3.2.bsb: And this is what he said:

Job.3.3.bsb: “May the day of my birth perish, and the night it was said, ‘A boy is conceived.’
Job.3.3.kjv: Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived.

Job.3.4.bsb: If only that day had turned to darkness! May God above disregard it; may no light shine upon it.
Job.3.4.kjv: Let that day be darkness; let not God regard it from above, neither let the light shine upon it.

Job.3.5.bsb: May darkness and gloom reclaim it, and a cloud settle over it; may the blackness of the day overwhelm it.
Job.3.5.kjv: Let darkness and the shadow of death stain it; let a cloud dwell upon it; let the blackness of the day terrify it.

Job.3.6.bsb: If only darkness had taken that night away! May it not appear among the days of the year; may it never be entered in any of the months.
Job.3.6.kjv: As for that night, let darkness seize upon it; let it not be joined unto the days of the year, let it not come into the number of the months.

Job.3.7.bsb: Behold, may that night be barren; may no joyful voice come into it.
Job.3.7.kjv: Lo, let that night be solitary, let no joyful voice come therein.

Job.3.8.bsb: May it be cursed by those who curse the day—those prepared to rouse Leviathan.
Job.3.8.kjv: Let them curse it that curse the day, who are ready to raise up their mourning.

Job.3.9.bsb: May its morning stars grow dark; may it wait in vain for daylight; may it not see the breaking of dawn.
Job.3.9.kjv: Let the stars of the twilight thereof be dark; let it look for light, but have none; neither let it see the dawning of the day:

Job.3.10.bsb: For that night did not shut the doors of the womb to hide the sorrow from my eyes.
Job.3.10.kjv: Because it shut not up the doors of my mother’s womb, nor hid sorrow from mine eyes.

Job.27.7.bsb: May my enemy be like the wicked and my opponent like the unjust.
Job.27.7.kjv: Let mine enemy be as the wicked, and he that riseth up against me as the unrighteous.

Job.12.4.bsb: I am a laughingstock to my friends, though I called on God, and He answered. The righteous and upright man is a laughingstock.
Job.12.4.kjv: I am as one mocked of his neighbour, who calleth upon God, and he answereth him: the just upright man is laughed to scorn.

Job.11.14.bsb: if you put away the iniquity in your hand, and allow no injustice to dwell in your tents,
Job.11.14.kjv: If iniquity be in thine hand, put it far away, and let not wickedness dwell in thy tabernacles.

Job.11.15.bsb: then indeed you will lift up your face without blemish; you will stand firm and unafraid.
Job.11.15.kjv: For then shalt thou lift up thy face without spot; yea, thou shalt be stedfast, and shalt not fear:

Job.34.31.bsb: Suppose someone says to God, ‘I have endured my punishment; I will offend no more.
Job.34.31.kjv: Surely it is meet to be said unto God, I have borne chastisement, I will not offend any more:

Job.8.4.bsb: When your children sinned against Him, He gave them over to their rebellion.
Job.8.4.kjv: If thy children have sinned against him, and he have cast them away for their transgression;

Job.11.16.bsb: For you will forget your misery, recalling it only as waters gone by.
Job.11.16.kjv: Because thou shalt forget thy misery, and remember it as waters that pass away:

Job.11.20.bsb: But the eyes of the wicked will fail, and escape will elude them; they will hope for their last breath.”
Job.11.20.kjv: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, and they shall not escape, and their hope shall be as the giving up of the ghost.

Job.22.21.bsb: Reconcile now and be at peace with Him; thereby good will come to you.
Job.22.21.kjv: Acquaint now thyself with him, and be at peace: thereby good shall come unto thee.

Job.22.22.bsb: Receive instruction from His mouth, and lay up His words in your heart.
Job.22.22.kjv: Receive, I pray thee, the law from his mouth, and lay up his words in thine heart.

Job.19.15.bsb: My guests and maidservants count me as a stranger; I am a foreigner in their sight.
Job.19.15.kjv: They that dwell in mine house, and my maids, count me for a stranger: I am an alien in their sight.

Job.19.16.bsb: I call for my servant, but he does not answer, though I implore him with my own mouth.
Job.19.16.kjv: I called my servant, and he gave me no answer; I intreated him with my mouth.

Job.20.12.bsb: Though evil is sweet in his mouth and he conceals it under his tongue,
Job.20.12.kjv: Though wickedness be sweet in his mouth, though he hide it under his tongue;

Job.20.13.bsb: though he cannot bear to let it go and keeps it in his mouth,
Job.20.13.kjv: Though he spare it, and forsake it not; but keep it still within his mouth:

Job.17.11.kjv: My days are past, my purposes are broken off, even the thoughts of my heart.

Job.28.7.bsb: No bird of prey knows that path; no falcon’s eye has seen it.
Job.28.7.kjv: There is a path which no fowl knoweth, and which the vulture’s eye hath not seen:

Job.16.18.bsb: O earth, do not cover my blood; may my cry for help never be laid to rest.
Job.16.18.kjv: O earth, cover not thou my blood, and let my cry have no place.

Job.20.9.bsb: The eye that saw him will see him no more, and his place will no longer behold him.
Job.20.9.kjv: The eye also which saw him shall see him no more; neither shall his place any more behold him.

Job.31.25.bsb: if I have rejoiced in my great wealth because my hand had gained so much,
Job.31.25.kjv: If I rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because mine hand had gotten much;

Job.8.8.bsb: Please inquire of past generations and consider the discoveries of their fathers.
Job.8.8.kjv: For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers:

Job.21.8.bsb: Their descendants are established around them, and their offspring before their eyes.
Job.21.8.kjv: Their seed is established in their sight with them, and their offspring before their eyes.

Job.32.21.bsb: I will be partial to no one, nor will I flatter any man.
Job.32.21.kjv: Let me not, I pray you, accept any man’s person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man.

Job.28.18.bsb: Coral and quartz are unworthy of mention; the price of wisdom is beyond rubies.
Job.28.18.kjv: No mention shall be made of coral, or of pearls: for the price of wisdom is above rubies.
